```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center", dpi = 150)

# Run all chunks from the repo root, so paths match the repo layout
# (data/..., analysis/...) whether knitted from RStudio or from a script.
repo <- system("git rev-parse --show-toplevel", intern = TRUE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = repo)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(ape)
  library(nlme)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(ggtree)
  library(aplot)
  library(ggrepel)
  library(mclust)

})
requireNamespace("Biostrings", quietly = TRUE)  # protein sequences in doubletrouble input files
source(file.path(repo, "scripts/nels.R"))  # nels_ls(), nels_read(), nels_file()

# Fetch input files that are not yet in data/, in one call to the shared
# downloader (scripts/download_files.sh, see CLAUDE.md).
fetch <- function(paths) {
  missing <- paths[!file.exists(file.path(repo, paths))]
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    status <- system2(file.path(repo, "scripts/download_files.sh"), shQuote(missing))
    if (status != 0) stop("Download failed for: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
  }
  invisible(paths)
}

# Figure and table numbers, in order of appearance
fig_ids <- c("contiguity", "nearident", "sd_contig", "landscape", "genes_dups",
             "ks_heat", "ks_peaks", "orth_ks",
             "dup_rate", "sd_share", "oxford", "asym", "exp_modes", "node_modes",
             "nb_age", "nb_same", "nb_events", "anc_ks")

             "nodes", "macro", "asym", "exp_modes", "nb_calib", "nb_nodes", "anc")

tab  <- function(id) paste("Table", match(id, tab_ids))
cap  <- function(id, text) paste0("**", fig(id), ".** ", text)
tcap <- function(id, text) paste0(tab(id), ". ", text)

order_levels <- c("Mortierellales", "Umbelopsidales", "Mucorales")
order_cols <- c(Mortierellales = "#E69F00", Umbelopsidales = "#009E73", Mucorales = "#0072B2")
mode_levels <- c("SD", "TD", "PD", "DD", "Near-identical")
mode_labs <- c(SD = "Segmental (SD)", TD = "Tandem (TD)", PD = "Proximal (PD)",
               DD = "Dispersed (DD)", "Near-identical" = "Near-identical (Ks < 0.05 or missing)")
mode_cols <- c(SD = "#D55E00", TD = "#CC79A7", PD = "#56B4E9", DD = "grey70",
               "Near-identical" = "grey20")
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 10) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

pct <- function(x, digits = 0) format(round(100 * x, digits), nsmall = digits)
```

# Background {-}

Corrochano et al. (2016, *Curr Biol* 26:1577) proposed a whole-genome
duplication (WGD) early in the Mucoromycotina. Their phylome contained four
Mucorales genomes with *Mortierella alpina* as the closest outgroup, so the
proposed WGD lies after the split from Mortierellales: between the
Umbelopsidales + Mucorales ancestor and the Mucorales ancestor. The evidence
was a burst of gene-tree duplications on that branch and larger gene families
than in Dikarya; there were few duplicated collinear regions, no 1:2 conserved
synteny with an outgroup and no Ks peak. The plan for this analysis is in
[`PLAN.md`](PLAN.md); each numbered section below follows one part of it.

## Duplicate classes (doubletrouble) {-}

Duplicate gene pairs were identified and classified within each genome with
doubletrouble (Almeida-Silva & Van de Peer), standard scheme. The definitions
below are from the source code of doubletrouble 1.8.1 (`classify_gene_pairs()`,
`classify_genes()`, `pairs2kaks()`) and its default parameters:

- **Paralogous pairs.** Each proteome is searched against itself with DIAMOND
  blastp (`syntenet::run_diamond()`: the top 5 hits per protein, one HSP per
  hit; the doubletrouble vignette adds `--sensitive`). Hits with E-value
  <= 1e-10 are kept, self-hits are removed, and A-B and B-A count as one pair.
  A gene is therefore "duplicated" if it has at least one significant
  paralogous hit, however old.
- **SD, segmental.** Anchor pairs in collinear blocks within the genome,
  detected by syntenet (MCScanX algorithm) with at least 5 anchor genes per
  block and up to 25 genes searched up- and downstream (`anchors = 5`,
  `max_gaps = 25`).
- **TD, tandem.** Remaining pairs on the same sequence that are adjacent in
  gene order.
- **PD, proximal.** Remaining pairs on the same sequence separated by 1 to 9
  genes (at most 10 positions apart, `proximal_max = 10`).
- **DD, dispersed.** All other pairs: on different sequences, or more than 10
  genes apart.
- **One mode per gene.** A gene in pairs of several modes is assigned the
  first in the order SD > TD > PD > DD (`classify_genes()`).
- **Ka and Ks.** Pairwise codon alignment and KaKs_Calculator rates
  (`MSA2dist::indices2kaks()`), model MYN by default. Recomputing Ks for 60
  random segmental pairs of AbsRepe with MYN reproduced the stored values
  exactly, so the default model was used. Ks is missing where it cannot be
  estimated, which is mostly the case for identical sequences (Section 1.2).

The DIAMOND and synteny settings of the original run are not recorded with the
data; the defaults above are assumed.

# Data {-}

The 61 genomes in the core analyses (dated species tree): Mortierellales,
Umbelopsidales and Mucorales. Input files are fetched from NeLS on first run.

```{r data}
fetch(c("data/metadata/genome_metadata_master.csv",
        "data/metadata/assembly_qc_summary.csv",
        "data/phylogeny/sco_cds_b500.date.nwk",
        "data/orthofinder/results/Comparative_Genomics_Statistics/Statistics_PerSpecies.tsv"))

md <- fread("data/metadata/genome_metadata_master.csv")
gen <- md[include_core_analyses == "yes",
          .(genome = tree_label, dt_id = genome_id, species = species_name, family,
            order = factor(order, order_levels))]
tree <- read.tree("data/phylogeny/sco_cds_b500.date.nwk")
stopifnot(setequal(gen$genome, tree$tip.label), !anyNA(gen$order))

# Number of protein-coding genes (OrthoFinder input proteomes)
ps <- fread("data/orthofinder/results/Comparative_Genomics_Statistics/Statistics_PerSpecies.tsv",
            header = TRUE, nrows = 10)
setnames(ps, 1, "stat")
ng <- unlist(ps[stat == "Number of genes", -1])
# OrthoFinder species names (e.g. AbsRepe_prot, gzAbsCyli1.proteins) by genome
of_names <- setNames(names(ng), sub("[._](prot|proteins|pep)$", "", names(ng)))
names(ng) <- names(of_names)
gen[, genes := as.numeric(ng[genome])]
stopifnot(!anyNA(gen$genes))

qc <- fread("data/metadata/assembly_qc_summary.csv")
gen[, busco_dup := qc$Busco_Dup[match(genome, qc$genome_id)]]

# Genomes in tree order (bottom to top), for plots
tip_data <- ggtree(tree)$data
tip_order <- with(tip_data[tip_data$isTip, ], label[order(y)])
```

```{r contig-lengths}
# Sequence lengths of every assembly. Computed once on NeLS (awk over each
# assembly FASTA, so the ~3 GB of assemblies are not downloaded) and saved to
# data/. This is the one NeLS-specific step; at publication the table is
# deposited with the other data files.
cl_path <- "data/genome_duplication/contig_lengths.tsv"
if (!file.exists(cl_path)) {
  remote <- paste(
    "cd", shQuote(nels_path("data/genomes")), "&& printf 'genome\\tseqname\\tlength\\n' &&",
    "for g in *; do",
    "f=$(ls \"$g\" | grep -E '\\.(fna|fasta|fa|fas)(\\.gz)?$' | grep -viE 'cds|transcript|protein|rna_from');",
    "[ $(echo $f | wc -w) -eq 1 ] || { echo \"No unique assembly in $g\" >&2; exit 1; };",
    "case \"$f\" in *.gz) r='gzip -dc';; *) r=cat;; esac;",
    "$r \"$g/$f\" | awk -v g=\"$g\" '/^>/ {if (n != \"\") print g \"\\t\" n \"\\t\" l; n = substr($1, 2); l = 0; next}",
    "{l += length($0)} END {if (n != \"\") print g \"\\t\" n \"\\t\" l}';",
    "done")
  dir.create(dirname(cl_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  writeLines(.nels_run(remote), cl_path)
}
cl <- fread(cl_path, colClasses = c(seqname = "character"))
stopifnot(all(gen$genome %in% cl$genome))
```

```{r gene-positions}
fetch(sprintf("data/genomes/%1$s/%1$s_genePosTbl.tsv", gen$genome))
gp <- rbindlist(lapply(gen$genome, function(g) {
  fread(sprintf("data/genomes/%1$s/%1$s_genePosTbl.tsv", g),
        colClasses = c(seqname = "character"))[, genome := g]
}))
gp <- merge(gp, cl, by = c("genome", "seqname"), all.x = TRUE)
stopifnot(mean(!is.na(gp$length)) > 0.99)  # gene tables and assemblies use the same names
```

```{r doubletrouble}
dup_files  <- sprintf("data/doubletrouble/dups/%s_dup.rds", gen$dt_id)
kaks_files <- sprintf("data/doubletrouble/kaks/%s_kaks.rds", gen$dt_id)
fetch(c(dup_files, kaks_files))

pairs <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(gen)), function(i) {
  d <- as.data.table(readRDS(dup_files[i]))
  k <- as.data.table(readRDS(kaks_files[i])[[1]])
  d <- merge(d, k[, .(dup1, dup2, Ka, Ks)], by = c("dup1", "dup2"), all.x = TRUE)
  d[, .(genome = gen$genome[i], dup1, dup2, type = as.character(type),
        seq1 = as.character(seqname1), seq2 = as.character(seqname2), Ka, Ks)]
}))
# Near-identical pairs: Ks < 0.05, or Ks not estimable (mostly identical
# sequences, see Section 1.2). These are recent duplicates or assembly
# duplicates and are kept apart from the older pairs.
pairs[, near_ident := is.na(Ks) | Ks < 0.05]
```

# Genome set and QC

## Assembly contiguity

Segmental duplicates can only be detected within assembled sequences, so a
fragmented assembly would show few SD pairs whatever its history. Contiguity
was computed the same way for every genome, from the assembly FASTA files and
the gene position tables.

```{r contiguity-calc}
n50 <- function(x) { x <- sort(x, decreasing = TRUE); x[which(cumsum(x) >= sum(x) / 2)[1]] }
asm <- cl[, .(n_seq = .N, size_mb = sum(length) / 1e6, n50_mb = n50(length) / 1e6), by = genome]
gcont <- gp[, .(gene_seqs = uniqueN(seqname), on_1mb = mean(length >= 1e6, na.rm = TRUE)),
            by = genome]
gen <- merge(gen, asm, by = "genome", all.x = TRUE)
gen <- merge(gen, gcont, by = "genome", all.x = TRUE)
```

```{r contiguity-fig, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 9, fig.cap = cap("contiguity", "Assembly contiguity of the 61 genomes, in species-tree order. Left: scaffold/contig N50 (log scale). Right: percentage of genes on sequences of at least 1 Mb, the sequences on which collinear blocks can be detected. Colour: order.")}
cont_long <- rbind(
  gen[, .(genome, order, metric = "N50 (Mb)", value = n50_mb)],
  gen[, .(genome, order, metric = "Genes on sequences >= 1 Mb (%)", value = 100 * on_1mb)])
cont_long[, metric := factor(metric, c("N50 (Mb)", "Genes on sequences >= 1 Mb (%)"))]
cont_long[, genome := factor(genome, tip_order)]
ggplot(cont_long, aes(value, genome, colour = order)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = scales::transform_pseudo_log(sigma = 0.1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = order_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Near-identical duplicates and assembly artifacts

Segmental duplicates here are collinear paralog blocks within one assembly
(see [Duplicate classes](#duplicate-classes-doubletrouble)). Two copies of the
same region in an assembly, for example uncollapsed haplotypes, also form
such blocks, but with identical or nearly identical genes.

```{r nearident-calc}
ni <- pairs[near_ident == TRUE]
ni_sd <- ni[type == "SD", .(ni_sd = .N, ni_sd_seq_pairs = uniqueN(paste(pmin(seq1, seq2), pmax(seq1, seq2)))),
            by = genome]
gen <- merge(gen, ni_sd, by = "genome", all.x = TRUE)
gen[is.na(ni_sd), `:=`(ni_sd = 0L, ni_sd_seq_pairs = 0L)]
gen <- merge(gen, pairs[, .(pairs = .N, ni_all = sum(near_ident),
                            sd_old = sum(type == "SD" & !near_ident)), by = genome],
             by = "genome")
```

```{r nearident-fig, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 9, fig.cap = cap("nearident", "Near-identical duplicate pairs (Ks < 0.05, or Ks not estimable) per genome and duplication mode, in species-tree order (pseudo-log scale). Many near-identical segmental pairs indicate duplicated stretches of the assembly or very recent segmental duplications.")}
ni_counts <- ni[, .N, by = .(genome, type)]
ni_counts[, `:=`(genome = factor(genome, tip_order), type = factor(type, mode_levels))]
ggplot(ni_counts, aes(N, genome, fill = type)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = scales::transform_pseudo_log(sigma = 1),
                     breaks = c(0, 10, 100, 1000)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mode_cols, labels = mode_labs, name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Near-identical duplicate pairs", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Ks cannot be estimated for identical sequences, but also not for some very
divergent ones. Protein sequences were compared for two genomes with many
segmental pairs without Ks (`r tab("identity")`).

```{r identity-check}
id_genomes <- c("gzMucFlav4", "gzMucCirc1")
id_files <- sprintf("data/doubletrouble/input_data/%s_data.rds",
                    gen$dt_id[match(id_genomes, gen$genome)])
fetch(id_files)
identity <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_along(id_genomes), function(i) {
  prot <- readRDS(id_files[i])$prot
  seqs <- setNames(as.character(prot), names(prot))
  p <- pairs[genome == id_genomes[i]]
  p[, identical_prot := seqs[dup1] == seqs[dup2]]
  p[, .(genome = id_genomes[i],
        mode = fifelse(type == "SD", "SD", "TD, PD, DD"),
        class = fcase(is.na(Ks), "Ks missing", Ks < 0.05, "Ks < 0.05", default = "Ks >= 0.05"),
        identical_prot)]
}))
stopifnot(!anyNA(identity$identical_prot))
id_tab <- identity[, .(pairs = .N, identical_protein_pct = round(100 * mean(identical_prot), 1)),
                   by = .(genome, mode, class)][order(genome, mode, class)]
id_sd_missing <- id_tab[mode == "SD" & class == "Ks missing"]
knitr::kable(id_tab, caption = tcap("identity", "Percentage of duplicate pairs with identical protein sequences, by mode and Ks class, in two genomes with many segmental pairs without Ks."))
```

```{r flags-table}
flag_tab <- gen[ni_sd >= 50 | (!is.na(busco_dup) & busco_dup > 5),
                .(genome, order, contigs = n_seq, N50_Mb = round(n50_mb, 2),
                  SD_pairs = ni_sd + sd_old, near_identical_SD = ni_sd,
                  sequence_pairs = ni_sd_seq_pairs, BUSCO_dup_pct = busco_dup)][order(-near_identical_SD)]
knitr::kable(flag_tab, caption = tcap("flags", "Genomes flagged for many near-identical segmental pairs (at least 50) or more than 5% duplicated BUSCO genes. sequence_pairs: number of distinct pairs of assembly sequences that carry the near-identical SD pairs. BUSCO values are available only for part of our own assemblies."))
```

## Contiguity and segmental duplicates

```{r sd-contig-fig, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = cap("sd_contig", "Segmental duplicate pairs with Ks >= 0.05 per 1,000 genes against the percentage of genes on sequences of at least 1 Mb. Each point is a genome; genomes with more than 20 pairs per 1,000 genes are labelled.")}
gen[, sd_per_1k := 1000 * sd_old / genes]
ggplot(gen, aes(100 * on_1mb, sd_per_1k, colour = order)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_text_repel(data = gen[sd_per_1k > 20], aes(label = genome), size = 3,
                  show.legend = FALSE, max.overlaps = 30) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = order_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Genes on sequences >= 1 Mb (%)", y = "SD pairs (Ks >= 0.05) per 1,000 genes")
```

```{r sd-contig-stats}
# Well-assembled genomes: at least 75% of genes on sequences >= 1 Mb. (The
# Umbelopsidales genomes are small, with chromosomes of 1-2 Mb, so a stricter
# cutoff would exclude all of them.)
hi_cont <- gen[on_1mb >= 0.75]
sd_by_order_hi <- hi_cont[, .(n = .N, median_sd_per_1k = median(sd_per_1k)), by = order][order(order)]
# Share of segmental pairs that are near-identical, per order
sd_ni_share <- pairs[type == "SD"][gen[, .(genome, order)], on = "genome", nomatch = NULL][
  , .(share = mean(near_ident)), by = .(genome, order)][, .(median_share = median(share)), by = order]
```

## Genomes of the same species

Several species are represented by more than one genome. These genomes are not
independent samples of duplicate content, and gene-tree duplications at their
common ancestor are likely to be noise (`r tab("strains")`).

```{r strains-table}
strains <- gen[, .(genomes = paste(sort(genome), collapse = ", "), n = .N), by = .(species, order)][n > 1][order(order, species)]
knitr::kable(strains[, .(species, order, genomes)],
             caption = tcap("strains", "Species represented by more than one genome."))
```

## Conclusion

```{r conclusion-1-values}
n_hi <- nrow(hi_cont)
flav4 <- gen[genome == "gzMucFlav4"]
mort_hi <- sd_by_order_hi[order == "Mortierellales"]
muc_hi  <- sd_by_order_hi[order == "Mucorales"]
umb_hi  <- sd_by_order_hi[order == "Umbelopsidales"]
```

- `r n_hi` of the 61 assemblies have at least 75% of their genes on
  sequences of 1 Mb or more (`r fig("contiguity")`), so collinear blocks can be
  detected in most genomes.
- Among these well-assembled genomes, segmental duplicates with Ks >= 0.05 are
  common in Mortierellales (median `r round(mort_hi$median_sd_per_1k, 1)` pairs
  per 1,000 genes, n = `r mort_hi$n`) and rare in Umbelopsidales
  (`r round(umb_hi$median_sd_per_1k, 1)`, n = `r umb_hi$n`) and most Mucorales
  (`r round(muc_hi$median_sd_per_1k, 1)`, n = `r muc_hi$n`)
  (`r fig("sd_contig")`). The exceptions are *Absidia* and *Rhizopus*. The
  scarcity of segmental duplicates in Mucorales and Umbelopsidales is
  therefore not an assembly artifact.
- In Mucorales, a large share of the few segmental pairs are near-identical
  (median `r pct(sd_ni_share[order == "Mucorales", median_share])`% of SD pairs
  per genome, against `r pct(sd_ni_share[order == "Mortierellales", median_share])`%
  in Mortierellales): recent segmental duplicates or duplicated assembly
  sequences rather than old collinear blocks.
- gzMucFlav4 has `r flav4$ni_sd` near-identical segmental pairs spread over
  `r flav4$ni_sd_seq_pairs` pairs of sequences in a `r flav4$n_seq`-sequence
  assembly, and `r id_sd_missing[genome == "gzMucFlav4", identical_protein_pct]`%
  of its segmental pairs without Ks have identical proteins (`r tab("identity")`).
  This points to duplicated (uncollapsed haplotype) sequences in the assembly.
  Near-identical pairs (Ks < 0.05 or missing) are kept as a separate category
  in all analyses below, and gzMucFlav4 should be checked before it is used in
  gene-count comparisons.
- `r nrow(strains)` species are represented by more than one genome
  (`r tab("strains")`); comparisons across genomes should treat them as one
  sample or use phylogenetic methods.

# Duplicate landscape per species

Each duplicated gene was assigned one mode, with the priority used by
doubletrouble's `classify_genes()`: SD > TD > PD > DD (definitions in
[Duplicate classes](#duplicate-classes-doubletrouble)). Near-identical pairs
were counted only for genes that are in no older pair.

```{r gene-modes}
gpairs <- rbind(pairs[, .(genome, gene = dup1, type, near_ident)],
                pairs[, .(genome, gene = dup2, type, near_ident)])
gpairs[, mode := fifelse(near_ident, "Near-identical", type)]
gpairs[, rank := match(mode, mode_levels)]
gmode <- gpairs[, .(mode = mode[which.min(rank)]), by = .(genome, gene)]
land <- gmode[, .N, by = .(genome, mode)]
land <- merge(land, gen[, .(genome, genes, order)], by = "genome")
land[, pct := 100 * N / genes]
land_wide <- dcast(land, genome + order + genes ~ mode, value.var = "pct", fill = 0)
for (m in mode_levels) if (!m %in% names(land_wide)) land_wide[, (m) := 0]
land_wide[, dup_pct := SD + TD + PD + DD]
```

```{r landscape-fig, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10, fig.cap = cap("landscape", "Duplicated genes per genome on the dated species tree. Middle: percentage of genes in each duplication mode (each gene counted once, priority SD > TD > PD > DD; near-identical only for genes in no older pair). Right: number of protein-coding genes. Tip colour: order.")}
tip_df <- data.frame(label = gen$genome, order = gen$order)
p_tree <- ggtree(tree) %<+% tip_df +
  geom_tippoint(aes(colour = order), size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = order_cols, name = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
p_modes <- ggplot(land[, .(genome, mode = factor(mode, rev(mode_levels)), pct)],
                  aes(pct, genome, fill = mode)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mode_cols, labels = mode_labs, name = NULL, breaks = mode_levels) +
  labs(x = "Genes (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
p_genes <- ggplot(gen, aes(genes / 1000, genome, fill = order)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = order_cols) +
  labs(x = "Genes (thousands)", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
p_modes %>% insert_left(p_tree, width = 0.5) %>% insert_right(p_genes, width = 0.35)
```

```{r orders-table}
ord_tab <- land_wide[, .(genomes = .N,
                         genes = median(genes),
                         duplicated = median(dup_pct), SD = median(SD), TD = median(TD),
                         PD = median(PD), DD = median(DD), near_identical = median(`Near-identical`)),
                     by = order][order(order)]
num <- names(ord_tab)[sapply(ord_tab, is.numeric)]
ord_tab[, (num) := lapply(.SD, round, 1), .SDcols = num]
knitr::kable(ord_tab, caption = tcap("orders", "Median number of genes and median percentage of genes in each duplication mode, per order."))
```

## Gene number and duplicated genes

Do genomes with more genes have more duplicated genes, and of which mode? The
slopes in `r tab("pgls")` are from phylogenetic generalised least squares
(Brownian motion on the dated tree), so related genomes are not counted as
independent.

```{r genes-dups-fig, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = cap("genes_dups", "Duplicated genes (excluding near-identical) against the number of genes, per duplication mode and in total. Each point is a genome; lines are ordinary least-squares fits across all 61 genomes, shown for orientation (phylogenetic fits in Table 5).")}
dup_counts <- dcast(land, genome + order + genes ~ mode, value.var = "N", fill = 0)
for (m in mode_levels) if (!m %in% names(dup_counts)) dup_counts[, (m) := 0]
dup_counts[, All := SD + TD + PD + DD]
dlong <- melt(dup_counts, id.vars = c("genome", "order", "genes"),
              measure.vars = c("All", "SD", "TD", "PD", "DD"), variable.name = "mode", value.name = "dup_genes")
dlong[, mode := factor(mode, c("All", "SD", "TD", "PD", "DD"),
                       c("All modes", mode_labs[c("SD", "TD", "PD", "DD")]))]
ggplot(dlong, aes(genes / 1000, dup_genes / 1000)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = order), size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~mode, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = order_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Genes (thousands)", y = "Duplicated genes (thousands)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r pgls}
pgls_fit <- function(y) {
  df <- as.data.frame(dup_counts[, .(genome, genes, y = get(y))])
  fit <- gls(y ~ genes, data = df, correlation = corBrownian(1, phy = tree, form = ~genome))
  ct <- summary(fit)$tTable
  data.table(mode = y, slope = ct["genes", "Value"], se = ct["genes", "Std.Error"],
             p = ct["genes", "p-value"])
}
pg <- rbindlist(lapply(c("All", "SD", "TD", "PD", "DD"), pgls_fit))
fmt_p <- function(p) vapply(p, function(x) format(signif(x, 2), scientific = x < 0.001), "")
pg_show <- pg[, .(mode, `duplicated genes per extra gene` = round(slope, 3),
                  SE = round(se, 3), p = fmt_p(p))]
knitr::kable(pg_show, caption = tcap("pgls", "Phylogenetic regression of the number of duplicated genes on the number of genes (61 genomes). The slope is the number of additional duplicated genes per additional gene."))
```

## Conclusion

```{r conclusion-2-values}
o <- function(ord, col) ord_tab[order == ord][[col]]
s <- function(m) pg[mode == m]
dd_share <- s("DD")$slope / s("All")$slope
sd_share <- s("SD")$slope / s("All")$slope
dup_range <- range(land_wide$dup_pct)
top_muc <- gen[order == "Mucorales"][order(-genes)][1:4]
top_sd <- top_muc[sd_per_1k > 20, genome]
top_other <- top_muc[sd_per_1k <= 20, genome]
```

Here "duplicated" means being in any paralogous pair that doubletrouble
detected (one of a gene's top 5 within-genome DIAMOND hits at E <= 1e-10),
which includes old and divergent paralogs.

- The duplicated fraction of the genome is similar across orders: median
  `r o("Mortierellales", "duplicated")`% of genes in Mortierellales,
  `r o("Umbelopsidales", "duplicated")`% in Umbelopsidales and
  `r o("Mucorales", "duplicated")`% in Mucorales (`r tab("orders")`). Most
  duplicated genes are dispersed in all three orders.
- Segmental duplicates make up a visible share only in Mortierellales
  (median `r o("Mortierellales", "SD")`% of genes) and in a few Mucorales
  genomes (*Absidia*, *Rhizopus*; `r fig("landscape")`); in most Mucorales and
  in all Umbelopsidales they are below 1%.
- Genomes with more genes have more duplicated genes
  (`r round(s("All")$slope, 2)` duplicated genes per additional gene,
  p = `r fmt_p(s("All")$p)`; `r tab("pgls")`). Dispersed duplicates account
  for about `r pct(dd_share)`% of that slope and segmental duplicates for
  `r pct(sd_share)`%, so variation in gene number is mostly variation in
  dispersed duplicates (`r fig("genes_dups")`).
- At the top of the range this differs: `r length(top_sd)` of the 4 Mucorales
  genomes with the most genes (`r paste(top_sd, collapse = ", ")`) have many
  segmental duplicates (more than 20 pairs per 1,000 genes); the other,
  `r paste(top_other, collapse = ", ")`, does not. This makes *Absidia* and
  *Rhizopus* candidates for lineage-specific WGDs (to be dated with Ks in
  Section 3).
- Mortierellales have more segmental, tandem and proximal duplicates and fewer
  dispersed ones than Mucorales of the same gene number, so their total
  duplicated fraction is similar (`r fig("genes_dups")`).

# Ks age distributions

Ks, the number of synonymous substitutions per synonymous site between the two
copies, grows with the age of a duplicate pair until it saturates at about
Ks 2, beyond which the estimates mostly reflect noise. A WGD leaves many pairs
of the same age, so a peak in the Ks distribution; small-scale duplication
leaves a smooth distribution of mostly young pairs. All pairs with
Ks >= 0.05 were used (near-identical pairs excluded); Ks values up to 5 are
shown, so that the saturated pairs are visible as their own group.

```{r ks-data}
ksd <- pairs[!near_ident & Ks <= 5]
ksd[, class := fifelse(type == "SD", "Segmental (SD)", "Small-scale (TD, PD, DD)")]
ksd <- merge(ksd, gen[, .(genome, genes, order)], by = "genome")
```

```{r ks-heat-fig, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10, fig.cap = cap("ks_heat", "Ks distributions of segmental (left) and small-scale (right) duplicate pairs per genome, in species-tree order. Colour: pairs per 1,000 genes in each Ks bin (log-spaced bins; square-root colour scale, separate for the two panels; white: no pairs). Pairs with Ks < 0.05 or without Ks are excluded. Dashed line: Ks = 2, above which Ks is saturated.")}
breaks <- seq(log10(0.05), log10(5), length.out = 41)
ksd[, bin := cut(log10(Ks), breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)]
heat <- ksd[, .(n = .N), by = .(genome, class, bin, genes)]
heat[, per_1k := 1000 * n / genes]
heat[, `:=`(x = (breaks[bin] + breaks[bin + 1]) / 2, genome = factor(genome, tip_order))]
heat_panel <- function(cl, show_y = TRUE) {
  ggplot(heat[class == cl], aes(x, genome, fill = per_1k)) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = log10(2), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = log10(c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5)),
                       labels = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "sqrt", name = "Pairs per\n1,000 genes") +
    labs(x = "Ks", y = NULL, title = cl) +
    theme(axis.text.y = if (show_y) element_text(size = 7) else element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = if (show_y) element_line() else element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5))
}
heat_panel("Segmental (SD)") + heat_panel("Small-scale (TD, PD, DD)", show_y = FALSE)
```

## Peaks in the segmental Ks distributions

Peaks were fitted with Gaussian mixture models (mclust, as in doubletrouble's
`find_ks_peaks()`), but on log Ks and over the range 0.05-5, so that the
saturated pairs get their own component instead of pulling a component
towards the cut-off. The number of components (1-4) was chosen by BIC. Only
genomes with at least 100 segmental pairs were fitted.

```{r ks-peaks}
fit_peaks <- function(ks) {
  m <- densityMclust(log(ks), G = 1:4, modelNames = "V", verbose = FALSE, plot = FALSE)
  o <- order(m$parameters$mean)
  data.table(component = seq_along(o), mean_log = m$parameters$mean[o],
             sd_log = sqrt(m$parameters$variance$sigmasq[o]), weight = m$parameters$pro[o])
}
sd_n <- ksd[class == "Segmental (SD)", .N, by = genome]
peak_genomes <- intersect(tip_order, sd_n[N >= 100, genome])
peaks <- rbindlist(lapply(peak_genomes, function(g) {
  fit_peaks(ksd[genome == g & class == "Segmental (SD)", Ks])[, genome := g]
}))
peaks[, Ks := exp(mean_log)]
# The main sub-saturation peak: the largest component with mean Ks < 2
main_peak <- peaks[Ks < 2][order(-weight)][, .SD[1], by = genome]
peak_tab <- peaks[, .(components = paste(sprintf("%.2f (%.0f%%)", Ks, 100 * weight), collapse = ", ")),
                  by = genome]
peak_tab <- merge(peak_tab, sd_n, by = "genome")
peak_tab <- merge(peak_tab, main_peak[, .(genome, main_Ks = round(Ks, 2), main_weight = round(weight, 2))],
                  by = "genome", all.x = TRUE)
peak_tab <- merge(gen[, .(genome, order)], peak_tab, by = "genome")[order(order, -main_weight)]
knitr::kable(peak_tab[, .(genome, order, SD_pairs = N, components, main_Ks, main_weight)],
             caption = tcap("peaks", "Gaussian mixture components of the log-Ks distribution of segmental pairs (Ks 0.05-5): component mean Ks and weight. main_Ks and main_weight: the largest component with mean Ks < 2."))
```

## Placing the peaks relative to speciation

A duplication peak is older than a speciation event if its Ks is larger than
the Ks between orthologs of the two species, and younger if it is smaller
(assuming similar substitution rates in the lineages). One-to-one orthologs
(OrthoFinder) were sampled for pairs of species that bracket the candidate
events, and Ks was computed in the same way as for the paralogs (MYN model;
400 random orthologs per pair). The comparisons with Umbelopsidales and
Mortierellales span the branches where Corrochano et al. placed their WGD.

```{r ortholog-ks}
orth_pairs <- data.table(
  a = c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "AbsRepe", "ggRhiOryz1", "ggRhiOryz1", "AbsRepe",
        "ggMorZona1", "ggRhiOryz1", "ggRhiOryz1"),
  b = c("AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1", "HalRadi", "gzRhiStol1", "gzRhiMicr1", "ggRhiOryz1",
        "gzPodHuml1", "gzUmbVina1", "ggMorZona1"),
  split = c("Within Absidia (A. cylindrospora / A. repens)", "Within Absidia (A. repens / A. glauca)",
            "Absidia / Halteromyces", "Within Rhizopus (R. oryzae / R. stolonifer)",
            "Within Rhizopus (R. oryzae / R. microsporus)", "Absidia / Rhizopus",
            "Mortierellales crown", "Mucorales / Umbelopsidales", "Mucorales / Mortierellales"))

orth_path <- "data/genome_duplication/ortholog_ks.tsv"
if (!file.exists(orth_path)) {
  load_cds <- function(g) {
    f <- sprintf("data/doubletrouble/input_data/%s_data.rds", gen[genome == g, dt_id])
    fetch(f)
    cds <- readRDS(f)$cds
    cds[Biostrings::width(cds) %% 3 == 0]  # as in pairs2kaks()
  }
  load_alias <- function(g) {  # any OrthoFinder identifier -> gene ID
    f <- sprintf("data/genomes/%1$s/%1$s_IDtbl.tsv", g)
    fetch(f)
    ids <- fread(f)
    unique(rbind(ids[, .(id = proteinID, gene = geneID)], ids[, .(id = rnaID, gene = geneID)],
                 ids[, .(id = geneID, gene = geneID)]))
  }
  # OrthoFinder separates genes with ", "; public FASTA headers carry descriptions,
  # so take the first word of each element that is a known identifier.
  known_id <- function(cell, known) {
    vapply(strsplit(cell, ", ", fixed = TRUE), function(p) {
      w <- sub(" .*", "", p); w <- w[w %in% known]
      if (length(w) == 1) w else NA_character_
    }, "")
  }
  n_genes_in <- function(cell) lengths(strsplit(cell, ", ", fixed = TRUE))
  ks_of_pairs <- function(cds_a, cds_b, ga, gb) {
    seqs <- c(cds_a[ga], cds_b[gb])
    names(seqs) <- c(paste0("a_", ga), paste0("b_", gb))
    idx <- lapply(seq_along(ga), function(i) c(i, length(ga) + i))
    r <- MSA2dist::indices2kaks(cds = seqs, indices = idx, model = "MYN", isMSA = FALSE,
                                threads = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1), verbose = FALSE)
    as.numeric(ifelse(r$Ks == "NA", NA, r$Ks))
  }
  ortholog_ks <- function(a, b, n = 400, seed = 1) {
    f <- sprintf("data/orthofinder/results/Orthologues/Orthologues_%1$s/%1$s__v__%2$s.tsv",
                 of_names[[a]], of_names[[b]])
    fetch(f)
    o <- fread(f, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, quote = "", col.names = c("og", "a", "b"))
    alias_a <- load_alias(a); alias_b <- load_alias(b)
    one <- o[n_genes_in(a) == 1 & n_genes_in(b) == 1]
    one[, `:=`(gene_a = alias_a$gene[match(known_id(a, alias_a$id), alias_a$id)],
               gene_b = alias_b$gene[match(known_id(b, alias_b$id), alias_b$id)])]
    cds_a <- load_cds(a); cds_b <- load_cds(b)
    one <- one[gene_a %in% names(cds_a) & gene_b %in% names(cds_b)]
    set.seed(seed)
    s <- one[sample(.N, min(n, .N))]
    data.table(a = a, b = b, one_to_one = nrow(one), gene_a = s$gene_a, gene_b = s$gene_b,
               Ks = ks_of_pairs(cds_a, cds_b, s$gene_a, s$gene_b))
  }
  orth_ks <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(orth_pairs)), function(i) {
    ortholog_ks(orth_pairs$a[i], orth_pairs$b[i])
  }))
  fwrite(orth_ks, orth_path, sep = "\t")
}
orth_ks <- fread(orth_path)
orth_ks <- merge(orth_ks, orth_pairs, by = c("a", "b"))
orth_sum <- orth_ks[, .(one_to_one = one_to_one[1], sampled = .N,
                        Ks_q25 = quantile(Ks, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), Ks_median = median(Ks, na.rm = TRUE),
                        Ks_q75 = quantile(Ks, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
                        saturated_pct = 100 * mean(Ks > 2, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(split, a, b)]
orth_sum <- orth_sum[match(orth_pairs$split, split)]
num <- c("Ks_q25", "Ks_median", "Ks_q75", "saturated_pct")
orth_sum[, (num) := lapply(.SD, round, 2), .SDcols = num]
knitr::kable(orth_sum, caption = tcap("orthks", "Ks between one-to-one orthologs of species pairs (400 random orthologs per pair; MYN model, as for the paralogs). one_to_one: number of one-to-one orthologs available. saturated_pct: percentage of orthologs with Ks > 2."))
```

```{r ks-peaks-fig, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = cap("ks_peaks", "Ks distributions of segmental pairs (Ks 0.05-5, log scale) in the genomes with the most segmental pairs: Absidia and Rhizopus (Mucorales) and two Mortierellales for comparison. Grey: histogram; black curve: fitted Gaussian mixture; coloured vertical lines: median ortholog Ks to the species named (Table 7). Dotted line: Ks = 2.")}
show <- c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1", "ggRhiOryz1", "gzRhiStol1", "ggMorZona1", "LinElon")
bw <- 0.1
hist_d <- ksd[genome %in% show & class == "Segmental (SD)"]
curves <- rbindlist(lapply(show, function(g) {
  p <- peaks[genome == g]; n <- hist_d[genome == g, .N]
  x <- seq(log(0.05), log(5), length.out = 300)
  y <- rowSums(sapply(seq_len(nrow(p)), function(i) p$weight[i] * dnorm(x, p$mean_log[i], p$sd_log[i])))
  data.table(genome = g, x = x, y = y * n * bw)
}))
ref_lines <- orth_ks[, .(Ks = median(Ks, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(a, b)]
ref_lines <- rbind(ref_lines[, .(genome = a, other = b, Ks)], ref_lines[, .(genome = b, other = a, Ks)])
ref_lines <- ref_lines[genome %in% show & other %in% c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1", "HalRadi",
                                                         "ggRhiOryz1", "gzRhiStol1", "gzRhiMicr1", "gzPodHuml1")]
ref_lines[, label := paste("vs", other)]
facet_lab <- function(g) paste0(g, " (", gen$species[match(g, gen$genome)], ")")
hist_d[, panel := factor(facet_lab(genome), facet_lab(show))]
curves[, panel := factor(facet_lab(genome), facet_lab(show))]
ref_lines[, panel := factor(facet_lab(genome), facet_lab(show))]
ggplot(hist_d, aes(log(Ks))) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = bw, boundary = log(0.05), fill = "grey75") +
  geom_line(data = curves, aes(x, y), linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log(2), linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_vline(data = ref_lines, aes(xintercept = log(Ks), colour = label), linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = log(c(0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5)), labels = c(0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Median ortholog Ks") +
  labs(x = "Ks", y = "Segmental pairs") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{r orth-ks-fig, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = cap("orth_ks", "Ks between one-to-one orthologs for each species pair (log scale; 400 orthologs per pair). Boxes: median and quartiles. Dotted line: Ks = 2. Red points: main segmental Ks peak (Table 6) of each Absidia and Rhizopus genome in the comparison.")}
orth_ks[, split_f := factor(split, rev(orth_pairs$split))]
pk_pts <- rbind(main_peak[, .(genome, Ks)][orth_pairs, on = c(genome = "a"), nomatch = NULL][, .(split, genome, Ks)],
                main_peak[, .(genome, Ks)][orth_pairs, on = c(genome = "b"), nomatch = NULL][, .(split, genome, Ks)])
pk_pts <- pk_pts[grepl("^(gzAbs|AbsRepe|ggRhi|gzRhi)", genome)]
pk_pts[, split_f := factor(split, levels(orth_ks$split_f))]
ggplot(orth_ks[Ks >= 0.01], aes(Ks, split_f)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, fill = "grey90") +
  geom_point(data = pk_pts, colour = "#D55E00", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(data = pk_pts, aes(label = genome), colour = "#D55E00", size = 2.8,
                  direction = "y", nudge_y = 0.3, min.segment.length = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5)) +
  labs(x = "Ks between orthologs", y = NULL)
```

## Conclusion

```{r conclusion-3-values}
mp <- function(g) main_peak[genome == g]
om <- function(s) orth_sum[split == s, Ks_median]
mort_main <- main_peak[genome %in% gen[order == "Mortierellales", genome]]
mort_sat <- ksd[class == "Segmental (SD)" & order == "Mortierellales", mean(Ks > 2)]
abs_rhi <- c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1", "ggRhiOryz1")
deep_sat <- orth_sum[split %in% c("Mucorales / Umbelopsidales", "Mucorales / Mortierellales"), range(Ks_median)]
mort_mid <- peaks[genome %in% gen[order == "Mortierellales", genome] & Ks > 1.5 & Ks < 3]
mort_high <- peaks[genome %in% gen[order == "Mortierellales", genome] & Ks >= 3]
lic <- mp("LicRamo"); lic_n <- sd_n[genome == "LicRamo", N]
```

- ***Absidia* and *Rhizopus oryzae* show clear Ks peaks.** The main
  segmental component lies at Ks
  `r paste(range(round(main_peak[genome %in% abs_rhi, Ks], 2)), collapse = "-")`
  and holds `r paste(pct(range(main_peak[genome %in% abs_rhi, weight])), collapse = "-")`%
  of the segmental pairs (`r tab("peaks")`, `r fig("ks_peaks")`): many
  collinear pairs of similar age, as expected after a WGD.
- **The two events are independent.** The *Absidia* and *R. oryzae* peaks are
  much younger than the split between the two genera (ortholog Ks
  `r om("Absidia / Rhizopus")`, saturated; `r fig("orth_ks")`).
- **The *Absidia* event is older than the split of *A. cylindrospora* and
  *A. repens*** (ortholog Ks `r om("Within Absidia (A. cylindrospora / A. repens)")`
  against peaks at `r round(mp("gzAbsCyli1")$Ks, 2)` and
  `r round(mp("AbsRepe")$Ks, 2)`), so it is shared by these two species.
  Whether it is shared with *A. glauca* is unclear: their ortholog Ks
  (`r om("Within Absidia (A. repens / A. glauca)")`) is close to the peak and
  near saturation, and *A. glauca* has far fewer segmental pairs.
- **The *R. oryzae* event is probably younger than its split from
  *R. microsporus*** (ortholog Ks `r om("Within Rhizopus (R. oryzae / R. microsporus)")`
  against a peak at `r round(mp("ggRhiOryz1")$Ks, 2)`; both near saturation,
  so this is tentative), consistent with the almost
  complete lack of segmental pairs in *R. microsporus*. It probably
  corresponds to the WGD reported for *R. delemar* (= *R. oryzae* lineage;
  Ma et al. 2009). Whether *R. stolonifer* shares it cannot be decided with Ks
  (ortholog Ks `r om("Within Rhizopus (R. oryzae / R. stolonifer)")`, close to
  both peaks); the gene trees in Section 4 show that it does.
- **Mortierellales segmental duplicates are mostly saturated.**
  `r pct(mort_sat)`% of their segmental pairs have Ks > 2, and most fall in
  components at Ks `r paste(sprintf("%.1f", range(mort_high$Ks)), collapse = "-")`. All `r uniqueN(mort_mid$genome)` Mortierellales
  genomes also have a smaller component at Ks
  `r paste(sprintf("%.1f", range(mort_mid$Ks)), collapse = "-")`
  (`r paste(pct(range(mort_mid$weight)), collapse = "-")`% of segmental pairs;
  `r tab("peaks")`). Its consistency across the order hints at an old shared
  event, but it lies at the edge of saturation, and the Mortierellales crown
  split is itself saturated (median ortholog Ks `r om("Mortierellales crown")`),
  so Ks cannot tell whether these duplicates predate the order.
- **A weaker signal in *Lichtheimia ramosa*.** LicRamo has a component at Ks
  `r round(lic$Ks, 2)` holding `r pct(lic$weight)`% of its `r lic_n`
  segmental pairs (`r tab("peaks")`). With so few pairs this is a candidate
  for a small, recent segmental event rather than evidence of a WGD.
- **Ks cannot date a WGD on the Mucorales or Mucoromycotina stem.** Orthologs
  between Mucorales and Umbelopsidales or Mortierellales have median Ks of
  `r paste(deep_sat, collapse = "-")`, almost all above 2, so any duplicate
  from that time is saturated too. Apart from *Absidia*, *Rhizopus* and the
  weak *L. ramosa* signal, no Mucorales or Umbelopsidales genome has a
  segmental Ks peak below saturation (`r fig("ks_heat")`). Testing the
  Corrochano et al. WGD needs the gene-tree and synteny approaches of part 4.

# Testing a WGD on the Mucorales / Mucoromycotina stem

Corrochano et al. placed the WGD after the split from Mortierellales, which in
our tree is either the branch leading to Umbelopsidales + Mucorales (node N9)
or the branch leading to Mucorales (N12). Four tests, each checked against the
two recent WGDs found in Section 3 (*Absidia* and *Rhizopus*) as positive
controls:

a. **Burst:** are gene-tree duplications unusually frequent on N9 or N12,
   given the length of the branch?
b. **Collinearity:** are the duplicates from that branch segmental pairs?
c. **1:2 macrosynteny:** does each chromosome of an unduplicated outgroup map
   to two chromosomes of a Mucorales genome?
d. **Copy number:** do gene families more often have two copies in Mucorales
   and one in the outgroup than the reverse, and are those families the ones
   duplicated on the branch? Are the duplications spread over many families,
   as after a WGD, or concentrated in a few, as in family expansions?

OrthoFinder assigns each gene-tree duplication to the species-tree node at
which both copies are inherited, so a duplication "at N12" happened on the
branch leading to N12. Only duplications with at least 50% support (both
copies retained in at least half of the descendant species; OrthoFinder's own
filter) are used.

```{r s4-nodes}
fetch(c("data/orthofinder/results/Species_Tree/SpeciesTree_rooted_node_labels.txt",
        "data/orthofinder/results/Gene_Duplication_Events/Duplications.tsv",
        "data/orthofinder/results/Orthogroups/Orthogroups.GeneCount.tsv"))
of_suffix <- "[._](prot|proteins|pep)$"
of_tree <- read.tree("data/orthofinder/results/Species_Tree/SpeciesTree_rooted_node_labels.txt")
of_tree$tip.label <- sub(of_suffix, "", of_tree$tip.label)
nt <- Ntip(of_tree)
depth <- node.depth.edgelength(tree)
root_age <- max(depth)

# OrthoFinder nodes within the 61 core genomes, matched to the dated tree by
# their descendant genomes (nodes where the two topologies differ get no match)
nodes <- rbindlist(lapply(c(seq_len(nt), nt + seq_len(of_tree$Nnode)), function(i) {
  tl <- if (i <= nt) of_tree$tip.label[i] else extract.clade(of_tree, i)$tip.label
  if (!all(tl %in% tree$tip.label)) return(NULL)
  m <- if (length(tl) == 1) match(tl, tree$tip.label) else getMRCA(tree, tl)
  if (length(tl) > 1 && !setequal(extract.clade(tree, m)$tip.label, tl)) m <- NA_integer_
  ords <- unique(as.character(gen$order[match(tl, gen$genome)]))
  data.table(node = if (i <= nt) tl else of_tree$node.label[i - nt], ntips = length(tl),
             dt_node = m, clade_order = if (length(ords) == 1) ords else "Several orders")
}))
nodes[, brlen := tree$edge.length[match(dt_node, tree$edge[, 2])]]
nodes[, age_end := root_age - depth[dt_node]]
nodes[, age_start := age_end + brlen]

dups <- fread("data/orthofinder/results/Gene_Duplication_Events/Duplications.tsv")
setnames(dups, c("og", "of_node", "gt_node", "support", "dup_type", "genes1", "genes2"))
dups[, node := sub(of_suffix, "", of_node)]
sup <- dups[support >= 0.5 & node %in% nodes$node]
nodes <- merge(nodes, sup[, .(dups = .N, ogs = uniqueN(og), single = mean(table(og) == 1)), by = node],
               by = "node", all.x = TRUE)
nodes[is.na(dups), `:=`(dups = 0L, ogs = 0L)]
nodes[, `:=`(rate = dups / brlen, per_og = dups / ogs)]

key_nodes <- data.table(
  node = c("N8", "N9", "N12", "N11", "N10", "N40", "N46", "N32"),
  label = c("Mucoromycota (root)", "Umbelopsidales + Mucorales", "Mucorales", "Umbelopsidales",
            "Mortierellales", "Absidia (3 species)", "A. cylindrospora + A. repens",
            "R. oryzae + R. stolonifer"))
# Internal branches long enough for a rate (very short branches between
# strains of one species give meaningless rates)
internal <- nodes[ntips > 1 & !is.na(brlen) & brlen >= 5]
med_rate <- median(internal$rate)
internal[, rate_rank := frank(-rate)]
```

## Duplication bursts

```{r dup-rate-fig, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = cap("dup_rate", "Gene-tree duplications (at least 50% support) on each internal branch of the species tree against the length of the branch in the dated tree (relative time units, root = 1,000; log scales). Dashed line: the median rate over all internal branches. Labelled: the branches where Corrochano et al. placed the WGD (N9, N12), the stems of the three orders, and the recent WGDs of Absidia and Rhizopus (positive controls).")}
lab_nodes <- merge(internal, key_nodes, by = "node")
ggplot(internal[dups > 0], aes(brlen, dups, colour = clade_order)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = log10(med_rate), slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_text_repel(data = lab_nodes, aes(label = paste0(node, ": ", label)), size = 3,
                  show.legend = FALSE, min.segment.length = 0, max.overlaps = 20) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(order_cols, "Several orders" = "grey40"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Branch length (relative time)", y = "Duplications on the branch") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Collinearity of the duplicates

Each gene-tree duplication splits a gene family into two sets of copies. Within
each descendant genome, all pairs of genes across the two sets were looked up
among the doubletrouble pairs, to see which mode they were classified as. A
WGD leaves many duplicates in collinear blocks, so a large share of segmental
pairs among the duplicates of one branch is the collinearity signal of a WGD.

```{r dup-genes}
fetch(sprintf("data/genomes/%1$s/%1$s_IDtbl.tsv", gen$genome))
alias_all <- rbindlist(lapply(gen$genome, function(g) {
  ids <- fread(sprintf("data/genomes/%1$s/%1$s_IDtbl.tsv", g))
  unique(rbind(ids[, .(id = proteinID, gene = geneID)], ids[, .(id = rnaID, gene = geneID)],
               ids[, .(id = geneID, gene = geneID)]))[, genome := g]
}))
# OrthoFinder writes genes as "<species>_<FASTA header>", with "." in the
# species name replaced by "_", separated by ", ". Pieces without a core-genome
# prefix are outgroup genes or parts of FASTA descriptions that contained ", ".
prefix <- data.table(genome = gen$genome, prefix = paste0(gsub(".", "_", of_names[gen$genome], fixed = TRUE), "_"))
sup_int <- sup[node %in% nodes[ntips > 1, node]]
sup_int[, event := .I]
gl <- rbind(sup_int[, .(event, node, side = 1L, x = genes1)], sup_int[, .(event, node, side = 2L, x = genes2)])
gl <- gl[, .(part = unlist(strsplit(x, ", ", fixed = TRUE))), by = .(event, node, side)]
gl[, genome := NA_character_]
for (i in seq_len(nrow(prefix))) gl[is.na(genome) & startsWith(part, prefix$prefix[i]), genome := prefix$genome[i]]
gl <- gl[!is.na(genome)]
gl[, id := sub(" .*", "", substring(part, nchar(prefix$prefix[match(genome, prefix$genome)]) + 1))]
gl <- merge(gl, alias_all, by = c("genome", "id"), all.x = TRUE)
gene_map_rate <- mean(!is.na(gl$gene))
gl <- gl[!is.na(gene)]

cross <- merge(gl[side == 1, .(event, node, genome, g1 = gene)], gl[side == 2, .(event, genome, g2 = gene)],
               by = c("event", "genome"), allow.cartesian = TRUE)
cross[, key := paste(pmin(g1, g2), pmax(g1, g2))]
cross <- unique(cross, by = c("genome", "key", "node"))
pair_key <- unique(pairs[, .(genome, key = paste(pmin(dup1, dup2), pmax(dup1, dup2)), type)], by = c("genome", "key"))
cross <- merge(cross, pair_key, by = c("genome", "key"), all.x = TRUE)
sd_node <- cross[, .(cross_pairs = .N, classified = sum(!is.na(type)), sd = sum(type == "SD", na.rm = TRUE)), by = node]
sd_node[, sd_share := sd / classified]
nodes <- merge(nodes, sd_node, by = "node", all.x = TRUE)
internal <- merge(internal, sd_node, by = "node", all.x = TRUE)
```

`r pct(gene_map_rate, 1)`% of the core-genome genes in the duplication
records were matched to gene IDs.

```{r sd-share-fig, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = cap("sd_share", "Percentage of segmental (SD) pairs among the doubletrouble pairs formed by the duplicates of each internal node, against the age of the node (relative time; root = 1,000). Only nodes with at least 100 classified pairs. Point size: number of classified pairs.")}
sdp <- nodes[ntips > 1 & !is.na(age_end) & classified >= 100]
ggplot(sdp, aes(age_end, 100 * sd_share, colour = clade_order)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = classified), alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(data = merge(sdp, key_nodes, by = "node"), aes(label = paste0(node, ": ", label)),
                  size = 3, show.legend = FALSE, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(order_cols, "Several orders" = "grey40"), name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 8, name = "Classified pairs", breaks = c(1000, 10000, 50000)) +
  labs(x = "Age of node (relative time)", y = "Segmental pairs (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

```{r nodes-table}
node_tab <- merge(key_nodes, nodes, by = "node", sort = FALSE)
node_tab <- merge(node_tab, internal[, .(node, rate_rank)], by = "node", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
node_tab <- node_tab[, .(node, label, genomes = ntips,
                         branch = ifelse(is.na(brlen), "root", sprintf("%.0f-%.0f", age_start, age_end)),
                         duplications = dups, rate = round(rate, 1),
                         rate_rank = ifelse(is.na(rate_rank), "", sprintf("%d of %d", rate_rank, nrow(internal))),
                         SD_pct = round(100 * sd_share, 1), dups_per_family = round(per_og, 2),
                         single_pct = round(100 * single))]
knitr::kable(node_tab, caption = tcap("nodes", sprintf("Key branches. branch: start-end age (relative time). rate: duplications per time unit (median over internal branches %.1f); rate_rank: among %d internal branches of at least 5 time units. SD_pct: segmental pairs among classified duplicate pairs. dups_per_family: duplications per gene family duplicated on the branch; single_pct: families duplicated only once on the branch.", med_rate, nrow(internal))))
```

## Macrosynteny between orders

The classical WGD test compares a duplicated genome with an unduplicated
relative: each region of the relative should match two regions of the
duplicated genome. This needs conserved synteny between the two. Chromosome
pairs sharing more one-to-one orthologs than expected (hypergeometric test,
BH-adjusted p < 0.05 and at least twice the expected number) were identified
between Hi-C assemblies, with *R. microsporus* against *R. oryzae* as the
control.

```{r macro}
load_alias <- function(g) alias_all[genome == g, .(id, gene)]
known_ids <- function(cell, known) {
  lapply(strsplit(cell, ", ", fixed = TRUE), function(p) { w <- sub(" .*", "", p); w[w %in% known] })
}
# All ortholog relations between two genomes, with positions and copy numbers
orthologs_pos <- function(a, b) {
  f <- sprintf("data/orthofinder/results/Orthologues/Orthologues_%1$s/%1$s__v__%2$s.tsv",
               of_names[[a]], of_names[[b]])
  fetch(f)
  o <- fread(f, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, quote = "", col.names = c("og", "a", "b"))
  o[, rel := .I]
  aa <- load_alias(a); ab <- load_alias(b)
  la <- o[, .(id = unlist(known_ids(a, aa$id))), by = rel][, gene := aa$gene[match(id, aa$id)]]
  lb <- o[, .(id = unlist(known_ids(b, ab$id))), by = rel][, gene := ab$gene[match(id, ab$id)]]
  la <- merge(la, gp[genome == a, .(gene = geneID, seq_a = seqname)], by = "gene")
  lb <- merge(lb, gp[genome == b, .(gene = geneID, seq_b = seqname)], by = "gene")
  la[, n_a := .N, by = rel]; lb[, n_b := .N, by = rel]
  merge(la[, .(rel, seq_a, n_a)], lb[, .(rel, seq_b, n_b)], by = "rel", allow.cartesian = TRUE)
}
macro_grid <- function(x, a, b) {
  big_a <- cl[genome == a & length >= 1e6, seqname]; big_b <- cl[genome == b & length >= 1e6, seqname]
  o1 <- x[n_a == 1 & n_b == 1 & seq_a %in% big_a & seq_b %in% big_b]
  total <- nrow(o1)
  g <- CJ(seq_a = unique(o1$seq_a), seq_b = unique(o1$seq_b))
  g <- merge(g, o1[, .N, by = .(seq_a, seq_b)], by = c("seq_a", "seq_b"), all.x = TRUE)
  g[is.na(N), N := 0L]
  g[, Na := sum(N), by = seq_a][, Nb := sum(N), by = seq_b]
  g[, `:=`(expected = Na * Nb / total, p = phyper(N - 1, Nb, total - Nb, Na, lower.tail = FALSE))]
  g[, padj := p.adjust(p, "BH")]
  g[, sig := padj < 0.05 & N >= 2 * expected]
  g[, `:=`(a = a, b = b, total = total)]
  g
}
macro_pairs <- data.table(a = c("gzRhiMicr1", "gzMucCirc1", "gzUmbVina1", "ggMorZona1"),
                          b = c("ggRhiOryz1", "ggRhiOryz1", "gzMucCirc1", "gzMucCirc1"))
macro_x <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(macro_pairs)), function(i) orthologs_pos(macro_pairs$a[i], macro_pairs$b[i]))
grids <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(macro_pairs)), function(i) macro_grid(macro_x[[i]], macro_pairs$a[i], macro_pairs$b[i])))
sp_short <- function(g) { s <- strsplit(gen$species[match(g, gen$genome)], " ")[[1]]; paste0(substr(s[1], 1, 1), ". ", s[2]) }
macro_tab <- grids[, .(one_to_one = total[1], in_linked_pct = round(100 * sum(N[sig]) / total[1], 1),
                       linked_pairs = sum(sig),
                       ref_chromosomes = uniqueN(seq_a[Na >= 50]),
                       median_partners = as.numeric(median(.SD[Na >= 50, sum(sig), by = seq_a]$V1))),
                   by = .(a, b)]
macro_tab[, comparison := paste(sp_short(a), "vs", sp_short(b)), by = .(a, b)]

# Control: do both R. oryzae copies of 1:2 orthologs fall on chromosomes
# linked to the R. microsporus chromosome?
ctrl <- grids[a == "gzRhiMicr1"]
linked <- ctrl[sig == TRUE, paste(seq_a, seq_b)]
big_b <- cl[genome == "ggRhiOryz1" & length >= 1e6, seqname]
r12 <- macro_x[[1]][n_a == 1 & n_b == 2 & seq_b %in% big_b][, if (.N == 2) .(both = all(paste(seq_a, seq_b) %in% linked)), by = rel]
ctrl_base <- sum(ctrl[sig == TRUE, N]) / ctrl$total[1]
knitr::kable(macro_tab[, .(comparison, a, b, one_to_one, linked_pairs, in_linked_pct, ref_chromosomes, median_partners)],
             caption = tcap("macro", "Macrosynteny between chromosome-level assemblies (sequences >= 1 Mb). linked_pairs: chromosome pairs with significantly more one-to-one orthologs than expected; in_linked_pct: percentage of one-to-one orthologs in those pairs; median_partners: median number of linked chromosomes of the second genome per chromosome of the first (chromosomes with at least 50 orthologs)."))
```

```{r oxford-fig, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8.5, fig.cap = cap("oxford", "Oxford grids of one-to-one orthologs between chromosomes (sequences >= 1 Mb, ordered by size) of two genomes. Colour: log2 of observed over expected orthologs; dots: significantly linked chromosome pairs. Top left: R. microsporus against R. oryzae, which had a WGD after their split (control).")}
grids[, `:=`(enrich = pmax(pmin(log2((N + 0.5) / (expected + 0.5)), 3), -3),
             panel = factor(paste(sp_short(a), "vs", sp_short(b)), macro_tab$comparison)), by = .(a, b)]
size_rank <- function(g, s) {  # rank of each chromosome by length (1 = largest)
  chroms <- cl[genome == g & seqname %in% s][order(-length), seqname]
  match(s, chroms)
}
grids[, `:=`(xa = size_rank(a[1], seq_a), yb = size_rank(b[1], seq_b)), by = .(a, b)]
ggplot(grids, aes(xa, yb, fill = enrich)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_point(data = grids[sig == TRUE], size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", name = "log2 obs/exp") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Chromosomes of first genome (by size)", y = "Chromosomes of second genome (by size)") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## Copy number in gene families

For each orthogroup, the median number of genes was taken over the genomes of
each group. Orthogroups present in both groups were counted as 2:1 (median 2
in the first group, 1 in the second) or 1:2. Without duplication on either
branch the two counts should be similar; a WGD in one group gives an excess of
2:1 families in that group (two-sided binomial test). The orthogroups were
also checked for supported gene-tree duplications on the stems of Mucorales
(N12), of Umbelopsidales + Mucorales (N9) and of Mortierellales (N10).

```{r asym}
cn <- melt(fread("data/orthofinder/results/Orthogroups/Orthogroups.GeneCount.tsv")[
  , c("Orthogroup", of_names[gen$genome]), with = FALSE], id.vars = "Orthogroup",
  variable.name = "of_name", value.name = "n")
cn[, genome := names(of_names)[match(of_name, of_names)]]
groups <- list(
  Mucorales = gen[order == "Mucorales", genome], Umbelopsidales = gen[order == "Umbelopsidales", genome],
  Mortierellales = gen[order == "Mortierellales", genome],
  "Absidia (A. cylindrospora, A. repens)" = c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe"),
  "Halteromyces + Cunninghamella" = c("HalRadi", "gzCunBlak1", "gzCunEchi1", "CunBert"),
  "Rhizopus (R. oryzae, R. stolonifer)" = c("ggRhiOryz1", "gzRhiStol1"),
  "R. microsporus" = c("gzRhiMicr1", "RhiMicr2"))
node_ogs <- function(nd) unique(sup[node == nd, og])
asym_test <- function(x, y) {
  m <- merge(cn[genome %in% groups[[x]], .(mx = median(n)), by = Orthogroup],
             cn[genome %in% groups[[y]], .(my = median(n)), by = Orthogroup], by = "Orthogroup")
  m <- m[mx >= 1 & my >= 1]
  r21 <- m[mx == 2 & my == 1, Orthogroup]; r12 <- m[mx == 1 & my == 2, Orthogroup]
  link <- function(ogs, nd) round(100 * mean(ogs %in% node_ogs(nd)))
  data.table(first = x, second = y, families = nrow(m), two_to_one = length(r21), one_to_two = length(r12),
             ratio = round(length(r21) / length(r12), 1),
             p = binom.test(length(r21), length(r21) + length(r12))$p.value,
             N12_in_2to1 = link(r21, "N12"), N9_in_2to1 = link(r21, "N9"), N10_in_1to2 = link(r12, "N10"))
}
asym <- rbindlist(list(
  asym_test("Absidia (A. cylindrospora, A. repens)", "Halteromyces + Cunninghamella"),
  asym_test("Rhizopus (R. oryzae, R. stolonifer)", "R. microsporus"),
  asym_test("Mucorales", "Umbelopsidales"), asym_test("Mucorales", "Mortierellales"),
  asym_test("Umbelopsidales", "Mortierellales")))
asym_show <- copy(asym)[, p := fmt_p(p)]
knitr::kable(asym_show, caption = tcap("asym", "Gene families with median copy number 2 in the first group and 1 in the second (two_to_one), and the reverse (one_to_two), among families present in both groups. The first two rows are the positive controls. N12_in_2to1, N9_in_2to1: percentage of the 2:1 families with a supported duplication on the Mucorales stem (N12) or the Umbelopsidales + Mucorales stem (N9); N10_in_1to2: percentage of the 1:2 families with a supported duplication on the Mortierellales stem (N10)."))
```

```{r asym-fig, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = cap("asym", "Number of gene families with median copy number 2:1 and 1:2 between two groups of genomes (log scale), with the ratio. The two recent WGDs (top) are positive controls.")}
asym_long <- melt(asym[, .(cmp = paste(first, "vs", second), two_to_one, one_to_two, ratio)],
                  id.vars = c("cmp", "ratio"), variable.name = "pattern", value.name = "families")
asym_long[, `:=`(cmp = factor(cmp, rev(unique(cmp))),
                 pattern = factor(pattern, c("one_to_two", "two_to_one"), c("1:2", "2:1")))]
ggplot(asym_long, aes(families, cmp, fill = pattern)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(data = asym_long[pattern == "2:1"], aes(x = families * 1.4, label = paste0(ratio, "x")),
            position = position_nudge(y = 0.2), size = 3, hjust = 0) +
  scale_x_log10(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("2:1" = "#0072B2", "1:2" = "#E69F00"), name = "First:second group") +
  labs(x = "Gene families", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Conclusion

```{r conclusion-4-values}
nv <- function(nd, col) nodes[node == nd][[col]]
ir <- function(nd) internal[node == nd, rate_rank]
ctrl_sd <- range(nodes[node %in% c("N40", "N46", "N32"), sd_share])
ctrl_rate <- range(nodes[node %in% c("N40", "N46", "N32"), rate])
ctrl_per_og <- range(nodes[node %in% c("N40", "N46", "N32"), per_og])
ctrl_age <- range(nodes[node %in% c("N40", "N46", "N32"), c(age_start, age_end)])
above <- internal[rate > nv("N12", "rate") & !node %in% c("N40", "N46", "N32")]
mort_early <- nodes[node %in% c("N10", "N13", "N19"), range(sd_share)]
mort_late <- nodes[clade_order == "Mortierellales" & ntips > 1 & age_end < 100 & classified >= 100, range(sd_share)]
a <- function(f, s, col) asym[first == f & second == s][[col]]
mt <- function(a_, col) macro_tab[a == a_][[col]]
conc_nodes <- internal[dups >= 500][order(-per_og)][1:2]
```

- **There is a duplication burst on the Mucorales stem (N12), not on N9.**
  N12 carries `r nv("N12", "dups")` supported duplications, a rate of
  `r round(nv("N12", "rate"), 1)` per time unit,
  `r round(nv("N12", "rate") / med_rate, 1)` times the median branch (rank
  `r ir("N12")` of `r nrow(internal)`; `r fig("dup_rate")`, `r tab("nodes")`).
  The only branches with higher rates are the recent WGDs of *Absidia* and
  *Rhizopus* (`r paste(round(ctrl_rate, 1), collapse = "-")`) and
  `r nrow(above)` short branches near the tips (`r paste(above$node, collapse = ", ")`;
  at most `r round(max(above$brlen))` time units long), where a few
  duplications give a high rate. The branch leading to Umbelopsidales +
  Mucorales (N9, `r round(nv("N9", "rate"), 1)`) and the Mortierellales stem
  (N10, `r round(nv("N10", "rate"), 1)`) are at the median. This places the
  Corrochano et al. event on the Mucorales stem, after the split from
  Umbelopsidales.
- **The burst is broad, like a WGD.** On N12, `r round(nv("N12", "per_og"), 2)`
  duplications per affected gene family, and `r pct(nv("N12", "single"))`% of
  the families are duplicated only once, as for the recent WGDs
  (`r paste(sprintf("%.2f", ctrl_per_og), collapse = "-")`), whereas bursts of
  family expansions concentrate in fewer families (for example
  `r conc_nodes$node[1]`, `r round(conc_nodes$per_og[1], 2)` per family).
- **The N12 duplicates show no collinearity, but the test is weak at that
  age.** `r pct(nv("N12", "sd_share"), 1)`% of their pairs are segmental,
  against `r paste(pct(ctrl_sd), collapse = "-")`% for the duplicates of the
  recent WGDs (`r fig("sd_share")`). Those WGDs happened on branches spanning
  `r round(ctrl_age[1])`-`r round(ctrl_age[2])` time units before present; the
  N12 branch spans `r round(nv("N12", "age_end"))`-`r round(nv("N12", "age_start"))`,
  at least twice as old, and gene order in Mucorales scrambles fast (synteny
  analysis). Collinear blocks from a WGD at N12 may therefore have been
  erased, so their absence does not rule it out.
- **No 1:2 synteny test is possible.** There is no macrosynteny between the
  orders: no chromosome pair of *M. zonata* or *U. vinacea* is linked to a
  *Mucor* chromosome (`r tab("macro")`, `r fig("oxford")`). Even the control is
  weak: each *R. microsporus* chromosome has a median of
  `r mt("gzRhiMicr1", "median_partners")` linked *R. oryzae* chromosomes, as
  expected after a WGD, but only `r mt("gzRhiMicr1", "in_linked_pct")`% of
  orthologs lie in linked pairs, and both copies of 1:2 orthologs fall on
  linked chromosomes in `r pct(mean(r12$both), 1)`% of cases against
  `r pct(ctrl_base^2, 1)`% expected by chance.
- **Gene families support extra copies from the Mucorales stem.** Mucorales
  have `r a("Mucorales", "Umbelopsidales", "ratio")` times more 2:1 than 1:2
  families relative to Umbelopsidales, and
  `r a("Mucorales", "Umbelopsidales", "N12_in_2to1")`% of these 2:1 families
  have a supported duplication on N12 (`r tab("asym")`, `r fig("asym")`). Each
  such family has two copies in at least half of the
  `r length(groups$Mucorales)` Mucorales genomes, so the duplicates were
  retained in parallel across the order. The excess is weaker than for the recent WGDs
  (`r paste(asym[1:2, ratio], collapse = " and ")` times), as expected after
  more gene loss, and part of it comes from gene loss in Umbelopsidales, which
  have the smallest gene sets and fewer 2:1 families than Mortierellales too
  (ratio `r a("Umbelopsidales", "Mortierellales", "ratio")`).
- **Gene trees resolve two questions from Section 3.** The *Rhizopus* burst
  maps to the branch before the split of *R. oryzae* and *R. stolonifer* (N32),
  so their duplications are shared. The *Absidia* burst is split between the
  branch before *A. glauca* diverged (N40) and the branch after it (N46), so
  part of it may be shared with *A. glauca*.
- **Mortierellales show their own early event.** Duplicates of the
  Mortierellales stem and the two following nodes (N10, N13, N19) are
  `r paste(pct(mort_early), collapse = "-")`% segmental, more than those of
  younger Mortierellales nodes (`r paste(pct(mort_late), collapse = "-")`%), and
  `r a("Umbelopsidales", "Mortierellales", "N10_in_1to2")`% of the families with
  more copies in Mortierellales than in Umbelopsidales trace to the
  Mortierellales stem. Collinear duplicates from early in the order are
  consistent with a large-scale duplication near the base of Mortierellales,
  matching the Ks component at 1.6-2.5 in all Mortierellales genomes
  (Section 3).
- **Overall:** our data agree with Corrochano et al. that there is an excess of
  duplications early in Mucorales, and place it on the Mucorales stem. Its
  breadth and the parallel retention of copies across Mucorales are what a WGD
  would leave, but the decisive evidence (collinear duplicates, 1:2 synteny)
  cannot be obtained, because gene order in Mucorales has been scrambled since.
  A burst of small-scale duplication combined with gene-tree errors at a deep
  node cannot be excluded with these tests. Section 6 revisits the
  collinearity test with a measure of synteny that does not depend on gene
  order.

# Copy number with microsynteny

A WGD adds copies to many gene families at once, in collinear blocks
(segmental duplicates while gene order is conserved, dispersed duplicates once
it has eroded). Small-scale duplication adds copies family by family, often
next to the original (tandem or proximal duplicates) or by transposition
(dispersed). Two views:

a. **Expanded families:** for gene families with more copies in a clade than
   in its sister group, what modes do the clade's genes have, compared with
   genes of families that are not expanded?
b. **Duplicates per branch:** what is the mix of modes among the duplicates
   that the gene trees place on each key branch (Section 4.2)?

```{r og-genes}
fetch("data/orthofinder/results/Orthogroups/Orthogroups.tsv")
og_tab <- fread("data/orthofinder/results/Orthogroups/Orthogroups.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = "")
# Genes of each core genome per orthogroup (cells list FASTA headers, ", "-separated)
og_genes <- rbindlist(lapply(gen$genome, function(g) {
  cell <- og_tab[[of_names[[g]]]]
  keep <- cell != ""
  l <- data.table(og = og_tab$Orthogroup[keep], cell = cell[keep])[
    , .(id = sub(" .*", "", unlist(strsplit(cell, ", ", fixed = TRUE)))), by = og]
  a <- alias_all[genome == g]
  unique(l[id %in% a$id][, .(og, genome = g, gene = a$gene[match(id, a$id)])])
}))
og_genes <- merge(og_genes, gmode, by = c("genome", "gene"), all.x = TRUE)
og_genes[is.na(mode), mode := "Not duplicated"]
dup_in_og <- mean(paste(gmode$genome, gmode$gene) %in% paste(og_genes$genome, og_genes$gene))
```

## Modes of genes in expanded families

A family is expanded in a clade if its median copy number there is at least 2
and at least one more than in the sister group; families present in both with
an equal or lower median in the clade are the background. Copy numbers are
the medians of Section 4.4. The genes of the clade's genomes in each set were
classified by their duplication mode (Section 2). `r pct(dup_in_og, 1)`% of
the duplicated genes are in an orthogroup.

```{r exp-modes}
exp_cmp <- data.table(
  x = c("Absidia (A. cylindrospora, A. repens)", "Rhizopus (R. oryzae, R. stolonifer)",
        "Mucorales", "Mucorales", "Mortierellales"),
  y = c("Halteromyces + Cunninghamella", "R. microsporus", "Umbelopsidales", "Mortierellales",
        "Umbelopsidales"))
group_median <- function(gs) cn[genome %in% gs, .(m = median(n)), by = Orthogroup]
mode_levels_all <- c(mode_levels, "Not duplicated")
exp_modes <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(exp_cmp)), function(i) {
  x <- exp_cmp$x[i]; y <- exp_cmp$y[i]
  m <- merge(group_median(groups[[x]]), group_median(groups[[y]]), by = "Orthogroup", suffixes = c("x", "y"))
  m <- m[mx >= 1 & my >= 1]
  sets <- list(Expanded = m[mx >= 2 & mx >= my + 1, Orthogroup], Background = m[mx <= my, Orthogroup])
  if (x == "Mucorales" && y == "Umbelopsidales") {
    sets[["Expanded, with N12 duplication"]] <- intersect(sets$Expanded, node_ogs("N12"))
  }
  rbindlist(lapply(names(sets), function(s) {
    g <- og_genes[genome %in% groups[[x]] & og %in% sets[[s]]]
    g[, .N, by = mode][, `:=`(comparison = paste(x, "vs", y), set = s, families = length(sets[[s]]),
                              genes = nrow(g), pct = 100 * N / nrow(g))]
  }))
}))
exp_wide <- dcast(exp_modes, comparison + set + families + genes ~ mode, value.var = "pct", fill = 0)
for (m in mode_levels_all) if (!m %in% names(exp_wide)) exp_wide[, (m) := 0]
exp_wide[, `:=`(local = TD + PD)]
exp_wide <- exp_wide[order(match(comparison, unique(exp_modes$comparison)), match(set, c("Background", "Expanded", "Expanded, with N12 duplication")))]
exp_show <- exp_wide[, .(comparison, set, families, genes, SD = round(SD, 1), `TD + PD` = round(local, 1),
                         DD = round(DD, 1), `Near-identical` = round(`Near-identical`, 1),
                         `Not duplicated` = round(`Not duplicated`, 1))]
knitr::kable(exp_show, caption = tcap("exp_modes", "Duplication modes (% of genes) of the clade's genes in gene families expanded in the clade relative to its sister group, and in background families. Each gene counted once (priority SD > TD > PD > DD; near-identical only for genes in no older pair). The first two comparisons are the positive controls."))
```

```{r exp-modes-fig, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = cap("exp_modes", "Duplication modes of genes in gene families expanded in a clade relative to its sister group (Expanded) and in families that are not (Background), for the two recent WGDs (positive controls, top) and the comparisons between orders.")}
em <- copy(exp_modes)
em[, `:=`(mode = factor(mode, rev(mode_levels_all)),
          set = factor(set, rev(c("Background", "Expanded", "Expanded, with N12 duplication"))),
          comparison = factor(comparison, unique(exp_modes$comparison)))]
ggplot(em, aes(pct, set, fill = mode)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(~comparison, ncol = 1, strip.position = "top", scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(mode_cols, "Not duplicated" = "grey92"), breaks = mode_levels_all,
                    labels = c(mode_labs, "Not duplicated" = "Not duplicated"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Genes (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 8)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

## Modes of the duplicates of each branch

```{r node-modes-fig, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = cap("node_modes", "Duplication modes of the doubletrouble pairs formed by the duplicates of each key branch (Section 4.2). The branches with the recent WGDs (N40, N46, N32) are positive controls; N26 (Linnemannia, a burst concentrated in few gene families, Section 4) is shown for comparison. n: classified pairs.")}
nm_nodes <- rbind(key_nodes[node != "N8"], data.table(node = "N26", label = "Linnemannia (family expansions)"))
nm <- cross[node %in% nm_nodes$node & !is.na(type), .N, by = .(node, type)]
nm[, pct := 100 * N / sum(N), by = node]
nm <- merge(nm, nm_nodes, by = "node")
nm_n <- nm[, .(n = sum(N)), by = .(node, label)]
nm[, lab := factor(paste0(node, ": ", label), rev(paste0(nm_nodes$node, ": ", nm_nodes$label)))]
nm_n[, lab := factor(paste0(node, ": ", label), levels(nm$lab))]
nm[, type := factor(type, rev(c("SD", "TD", "PD", "DD")))]
ggplot(nm, aes(pct, lab, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(data = nm_n, aes(x = 101, y = lab, label = paste0("n = ", format(n, big.mark = ","))),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mode_cols, breaks = c("SD", "TD", "PD", "DD"),
                    labels = mode_labs[c("SD", "TD", "PD", "DD")], name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 118), breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Classified duplicate pairs (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
node_modes <- dcast(nm, node ~ type, value.var = "pct", fill = 0)
```

## Conclusion

```{r conclusion-5-values}
ew <- function(cmp, s, col) exp_wide[comparison == cmp & set == s][[col]]
c_abs <- "Absidia (A. cylindrospora, A. repens) vs Halteromyces + Cunninghamella"
c_rhi <- "Rhizopus (R. oryzae, R. stolonifer) vs R. microsporus"
c_mu <- "Mucorales vs Umbelopsidales"; c_mm <- "Mucorales vs Mortierellales"; c_mo <- "Mortierellales vs Umbelopsidales"
f1 <- function(v) sprintf("%.1f", v)
nmod <- function(nd, ty) round(node_modes[node == nd][[ty]], 1)
```

- **Controls.** In families expanded in *Absidia* and *Rhizopus*,
  `r f1(ew(c_abs, "Expanded", "SD"))`% and `r f1(ew(c_rhi, "Expanded", "SD"))`%
  of the genes are segmental duplicates, against
  `r f1(ew(c_abs, "Background", "SD"))`% and `r f1(ew(c_rhi, "Background", "SD"))`%
  in background families, while tandem and proximal duplicates stay below
  `r f1(max(ew(c_abs, "Expanded", "local"), ew(c_rhi, "Expanded", "local")))`%
  (`r tab("exp_modes")`, `r fig("exp_modes")`): expansions by WGD, still in
  collinear blocks.
- **Mucorales expansions are dispersed.** Of the genes in families expanded in
  Mucorales relative to Umbelopsidales, `r f1(ew(c_mu, "Expanded", "DD"))`% are
  dispersed duplicates, only `r f1(ew(c_mu, "Expanded", "SD"))`% segmental and
  `r f1(ew(c_mu, "Expanded", "local"))`% tandem or proximal (similar for
  Mucorales against Mortierellales). For the expanded families with a
  duplication on the Mucorales stem the figures are
  `r f1(ew(c_mu, "Expanded, with N12 duplication", "DD"))`%,
  `r f1(ew(c_mu, "Expanded, with N12 duplication", "SD"))`% and
  `r f1(ew(c_mu, "Expanded, with N12 duplication", "local"))`%, and the
  duplicates mapped to N12 itself are `r nmod("N12", "DD")`% dispersed and
  `r nmod("N12", "TD") + nmod("N12", "PD")`% tandem or proximal
  (`r fig("node_modes")`), whereas the duplicates of the *Linnemannia* burst of
  family expansions (N26) are `r nmod("N26", "TD") + nmod("N26", "PD")`%
  tandem or proximal. The extra Mucorales copies are thus not the product of
  local tandem expansions; they are scattered across the genome, which is
  what an old WGD looks like after gene order has been scrambled, but also
  what dispersed (e.g. transposition-mediated) duplication produces.
- **Mortierellales expansions are collinear.** Families expanded in
  Mortierellales relative to Umbelopsidales are
  `r f1(ew(c_mo, "Expanded", "SD"))`% segmental
  (background `r f1(ew(c_mo, "Background", "SD"))`%) and
  `r f1(ew(c_mo, "Expanded", "local"))`% tandem or proximal, and the duplicates
  of the Mortierellales stem (N10) are `r nmod("N10", "SD")`% segmental. This
  supports a large-scale duplication early in Mortierellales (Section 4), with
  some tandem expansion on top.
- **Microsynteny therefore cannot separate the two explanations for the
  Mucorales stem burst.** Its duplicates look like those of a WGD whose blocks
  have eroded, and unlike tandem family expansions, but dispersed small-scale
  duplication would look the same, as long as segmental duplicates are
  defined by collinearity. Section 6 uses a definition that tolerates
  scrambled gene order.

# Order-free synteny of duplicates

doubletrouble calls a pair segmental only if it is an anchor of a collinear
block: at least 5 paralog pairs in the same order, with gaps of at most 25
genes. Gene order within chromosomes is scrambled much faster in Mucorales and
Umbelopsidales than in Mortierellales (synteny analysis), which breaks blocks
into pieces too short for this rule even when the duplicated regions still
share their gene content. A duplicate pair that arose in a segmental duplication
or WGD is then classified as dispersed. If so, the same ancestral duplication
can be segmental in one genome and dispersed in another.

**Neighbourhood synteny.** For each paralog pair (A, B), the genes within
W genes of A and of B were compared, ignoring order and orientation. The
support of the pair is the number of different gene families (orthogroups,
other than the family of A and B) with a paralog pair linking a gene near A
to a gene near B. A pair is *neighbourhood-syntenic* if its support reaches a
threshold k, i.e. A and B lie in regions that were duplicated together with
genes of at least k other families. Near-identical pairs were excluded as
pairs and as support, and pairs whose neighbourhoods overlap (closer than 2W
genes on one sequence) were not tested. The rate expected by chance was
measured by repeating the test after shuffling gene order in each genome
(3 shuffles). The main setting is W = 10, k = 2; W = 20, k = 3 and
W = 30, k = 4 have similar chance rates and are used to check robustness.

```{r nbhd-support}
nb_path <- "data/genome_duplication/neighbourhood_support.tsv.gz"
nb_k <- c(`10` = 2, `20` = 3, `30` = 4)
if (!file.exists(nb_path)) {
  nbhd_support <- function(pp, ord, fam, W) {
    pp <- merge(pp, ord[, .(a = gene, sa = seq, ra = rank)], by = "a")
