    pp <- merge(pp, ord[, .(b = gene, sb = seq, rb = rank)], by = "b")
    pp[, `:=`(fam_ab = fam[a], tested = !(sa == sb & abs(ra - rb) <= 2 * W))]
    links <- rbind(pp[, .(x = a, y = b, sx = sa, rx = ra, sy = sb, ry = rb)],
                   pp[, .(x = b, y = a, sx = sb, rx = rb, sy = sa, ry = ra)])
    links[, fam_xy := fam[x]]
    foc <- pp[tested == TRUE, .(a, b, sa, sb, fam_ab, alo = ra - W, ahi = ra + W, blo = rb - W, bhi = rb + W)]
    j <- links[foc, on = .(sx == sa, rx >= alo, rx <= ahi, sy == sb, ry >= blo, ry <= bhi),
               nomatch = NULL, allow.cartesian = TRUE, .(a = i.a, b = i.b, x, y, fam_xy, fam_ab = i.fam_ab)]
    j <- j[x != a & y != b & x != b & y != a & (is.na(fam_xy) | is.na(fam_ab) | fam_xy != fam_ab)]
    j[is.na(fam_xy), fam_xy := paste0("gene:", pmin(x, y))]
    s <- j[, .(support = uniqueN(fam_xy)), by = .(a, b)]
    out <- merge(pp[tested == TRUE, .(a, b)], s, by = c("a", "b"), all.x = TRUE)
    out[is.na(support), support := 0L]
    out
  }
  nb <- rbindlist(lapply(gen$genome, function(g) {
    pp <- pairs[genome == g & !near_ident, .(a = dup1, b = dup2)]
    ord <- unique(gp[genome == g, .(gene = geneID, seq = seqname, start)], by = "gene")
    setorder(ord, seq, start)
    ord[, rank := seq_len(.N), by = seq]
    fam <- og_genes[genome == g, setNames(og, gene)]
    rbindlist(lapply(as.numeric(names(nb_k)), function(W) {
      runs <- list(real = ord)
      for (s in 1:3) { set.seed(s); o <- copy(ord); o[, gene := sample(gene)]; runs[[paste0("null", s)]] <- o }
      rbindlist(lapply(names(runs), function(r) nbhd_support(pp, runs[[r]], fam, W)[, `:=`(W = W, run = r)]))
    }))[, genome := g]
  }))
  fwrite(nb, nb_path, sep = "\t")
}
nb <- fread(nb_path)
nb[, `:=`(key = paste(pmin(a, b), pmax(a, b)), pass = support >= nb_k[as.character(W)], is_null = run != "real")]
nb <- merge(nb, pair_key, by = c("genome", "key"), all.x = TRUE)
nb <- merge(nb, gen[, .(genome, order)], by = "genome")
```

## Calibration

```{r nb-calib}
calib <- nb[, .(chance = 100 * mean(pass[is_null]), real = 100 * mean(pass[!is_null]),
                SD = 100 * mean(pass[!is_null & type == "SD"]), DD = 100 * mean(pass[!is_null & type == "DD"])),
            by = .(W, k = nb_k[as.character(W)], order)][order(W, order)]
calib[, DD_over_chance := DD / chance]
num <- c("chance", "real", "SD", "DD", "DD_over_chance")
calib_show <- copy(calib)[, (num) := lapply(.SD, function(v) signif(v, 3)), .SDcols = num]
knitr::kable(calib_show, caption = tcap("nb_calib", "Percentage of tested paralog pairs that are neighbourhood-syntenic, by setting (window W, threshold k) and order: in genomes with shuffled gene order (chance), in the real genomes (real), and among doubletrouble's segmental (SD) and dispersed (DD) pairs. DD_over_chance: dispersed pairs passing relative to chance."))
```

## Neighbourhood synteny of the duplicates of each branch

```{r nb-nodes}
nbx <- merge(cross[, .(genome, key, node, event)], nb[, .(genome, key, W, run, is_null, pass)],
             by = c("genome", "key"))
nb_node <- nbx[, .(tested = sum(!is_null) / 1, real = 100 * mean(pass[!is_null]), chance = 100 * mean(pass[is_null])),
               by = .(node, W)]
nb_node[, tested := tested]
nb_ev <- nbx[W == 10, .(any = any(pass)), by = .(node, event, run)][
  , .(events = sum(run == "real"), ev_real = 100 * mean(any[run == "real"]), ev_chance = 100 * mean(any[run != "real"])), by = node]
nb_w <- dcast(nb_node, node ~ W, value.var = c("real", "chance", "tested"))
nb_w <- merge(nb_w, nb_ev, by = "node")
nb_w <- merge(nb_w, nodes[, .(node, ntips, clade_order, age_start, age_end)], by = "node")
```

```{r nb-age-fig, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = cap("nb_age", "Percentage of neighbourhood-syntenic pairs (W = 10, k = 2) among the duplicates of each internal node against the age of the node (square-root scale). Nodes with at least 200 tested pairs. Dashed line: rate in genomes with shuffled gene order. Compare with the collinearity-based Figure 10.")}
nba <- nb_w[ntips > 1 & !is.na(age_end) & tested_10 >= 200]
nb_chance <- nb[W == 10 & is_null == TRUE, 100 * mean(pass)]
ggplot(nba, aes(age_end, real_10, colour = clade_order)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = nb_chance, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = tested_10), alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(data = merge(nba, key_nodes, by = "node"), aes(label = paste0(node, ": ", label)),
                  size = 3, show.legend = FALSE, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_y_sqrt(breaks = c(0.2, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(order_cols, "Several orders" = "grey40"), name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 8, name = "Tested pairs", breaks = c(1000, 10000, 50000)) +
  labs(x = "Age of node (relative time)", y = "Neighbourhood-syntenic pairs (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

```{r nb-nodes-table}
nb_tab <- merge(key_nodes[node != "N8"], nb_w, by = "node", sort = FALSE)
nb_tab <- merge(nb_tab, nodes[, .(node, sd_share)], by = "node", sort = FALSE)
nb_tab <- nb_tab[, .(node, label, tested = tested_10, collinear_SD = round(100 * sd_share, 1),
                     syntenic = round(real_10, 1), chance = round(chance_10, 2),
                     enrichment = round(real_10 / chance_10), syntenic_W20 = round(real_20, 1),
                     syntenic_W30 = round(real_30, 1), events, events_syntenic = round(ev_real, 1),
                     events_chance = round(ev_chance, 1))]
knitr::kable(nb_tab, caption = tcap("nb_nodes", "Neighbourhood synteny of the duplicates of key branches. tested: duplicate pairs tested (W = 10). collinear_SD: % segmental pairs by doubletrouble's collinearity rule (Section 4.2). syntenic, chance: % neighbourhood-syntenic pairs (W = 10, k = 2) in the real genomes and with shuffled gene order; syntenic_W20, syntenic_W30: the same with W = 20, k = 3 and W = 30, k = 4. events_syntenic: % of the gene-tree duplications with a neighbourhood-syntenic pair in at least one descendant genome; events_chance: the same with shuffled gene order."))
```

## Same genomes, different ages

Gene order is scrambled at different rates in different genomes, so the
duplicates of different branches are best compared within the same genomes.
For each younger Mucorales node, the genomes below it were taken, and the
neighbourhood synteny of the node's own duplicates was compared with that of
the Mucorales-stem (N12) and N9 duplicates in the same genomes. Synteny only
decays with time, so older duplicates that are more often syntenic than
younger ones must more often have arisen in multi-gene (segmental or
whole-genome) duplications.

```{r nb-same}
of_desc <- function(nd) extract.clade(of_tree, nt + match(nd, of_tree$node.label))$tip.label
real10 <- nbx[W == 10 & !is_null]
young <- nodes[clade_order == "Mucorales" & ntips > 2 & !is.na(age_end) & age_end < nv("N12", "age_end")]
same <- rbindlist(lapply(young$node, function(nd) {
  gs <- of_desc(nd); y <- real10[genome %in% gs]
  data.table(node = nd, genomes = length(gs), own_n = y[node == nd, .N],
             own = 100 * y[node == nd, mean(pass)], N12 = 100 * y[node == "N12", mean(pass)],
             N9 = 100 * y[node == "N9", mean(pass)])
}))[own_n >= 200]
same <- merge(same, nodes[, .(node, age_start, age_end)], by = "node")
# nodes on or next to the branches of the recent WGDs and the Lichtheimia signal
wgd_linked <- c("N40", "N23", "N31", "N45", "N37")
same[, group := fifelse(node %in% wgd_linked, "Near a recent WGD or the Lichtheimia signal", "Other")]
same[, lab := sprintf("%s (%.0f-%.0f; %d genomes)", node, age_end, age_start, genomes)]
same <- same[order(-age_start)]
```

```{r nb-same-fig, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = cap("nb_same", "Neighbourhood-syntenic pairs (%) among the duplicates of younger Mucorales nodes (own) and among the Mucorales-stem (N12) and N9 duplicates in the same genomes. Each row: one node, with its age range (relative time) and the number of genomes below it. Rows marked with an asterisk are nodes on or next to the branches of the recent Absidia and Rhizopus WGDs or the Lichtheimia signal.")}
sl <- melt(same[, .(lab, group, own, N12, N9)], id.vars = c("lab", "group"), variable.name = "dups", value.name = "pct")
sl[, lab := factor(ifelse(group == "Other", lab, paste0(lab, " *")),
                   rev(ifelse(same$group == "Other", same$lab, paste0(same$lab, " *"))))]
sl[, dups := factor(dups, c("own", "N12", "N9"), c("Own duplicates (younger)", "N12 duplicates (Mucorales stem)", "N9 duplicates"))]
ggplot(sl, aes(pct, lab)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = lab), colour = "grey80") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = dups), size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_sqrt(breaks = c(0.5, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey50", "#0072B2", "#E69F00"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Neighbourhood-syntenic pairs (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Mucorales-stem duplications across genomes

```{r nb-events-fig, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = cap("nb_events", "Left: number of Mucorales genomes in which a Mucorales-stem (N12) duplication has a neighbourhood-syntenic pair, for the real genomes and with shuffled gene order (mean of 3 shuffles); duplications syntenic in no genome are not shown. Right: neighbourhood-syntenic pairs (%) among the N12 duplicates in each Mucorales genome, in species-tree order.")}
ev12 <- nbx[W == 10 & node == "N12", .(n_genomes = uniqueN(genome[pass])), by = .(event, run)]
ev12[, bin := cut(n_genomes, c(0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, Inf), labels = c("1", "2", "3-5", "6-10", "11-20", ">20"))]
evh <- ev12[n_genomes > 0, .N, by = .(bin, real = run == "real")][, N := ifelse(real, N, N / 3)]
evh[, set := factor(ifelse(real, "Real genomes", "Shuffled gene order"), c("Real genomes", "Shuffled gene order"))]
p_ev <- ggplot(evh, aes(bin, N, fill = set)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#0072B2", "grey70"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Genomes in which the duplication is syntenic", y = "N12 duplications") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
g12 <- real10[node == "N12", .(pct = 100 * mean(pass), n = .N), by = genome]
g12[, genome := factor(genome, tip_order)]
p_g <- ggplot(g12, aes(pct, genome)) +
  geom_col(fill = order_cols[["Mucorales"]], width = 0.75) +
  labs(x = "Syntenic N12 pairs (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5))
p_ev + p_g + plot_layout(widths = c(1.3, 1))
```

## Ancestrally segmental duplications (ancientSD) and their Ks

A gene-tree duplication is *ancestrally segmental* (ancientSD) if, in at least
two descendant genomes, one of its duplicate pairs is segmental (doubletrouble)
or neighbourhood-syntenic (W = 10, k = 2). All pairs of such a duplication,
in every descendant genome, are then counted as ancientSD, including those now
classified as dispersed: the duplication arose in a block, whatever its state
today. Requiring two genomes keeps chance passes rare (Section 6.4). Their Ks
distributions show whether these block duplications can be dated.

```{r anc-class}
nb_real10 <- nb[W == 10 & !is_null, .(genome, key, nb_pass = pass)]
anc <- merge(cross[, .(genome, key, node, event, type)], nb_real10, by = c("genome", "key"), all.x = TRUE)
anc[, syn := type %in% "SD" | (!is.na(nb_pass) & nb_pass)]
anc <- merge(anc, anc[, .(syn_genomes = uniqueN(genome[syn])), by = event], by = "event")
anc[, cls := fcase(syn_genomes >= 2, "ancientSD", syn_genomes == 1, "Syntenic in 1 genome",
                   default = "No synteny")]
pair_ks <- unique(pairs[, .(genome, key = paste(pmin(dup1, dup2), pmax(dup1, dup2)), Ks)], by = c("genome", "key"))
anc <- merge(anc, pair_ks, by = c("genome", "key"), all.x = TRUE)
anc_nodes <- key_nodes[node != "N8"]
anc_ev <- unique(anc[, .(event, node, cls)])[node %in% anc_nodes$node,
  .(events = .N, ancientSD = sum(cls == "ancientSD")), by = node]
ksw <- anc[node %in% anc_nodes$node & !is.na(Ks) & Ks >= 0.05 & Ks <= 5]
ksw[, set := fifelse(cls == "ancientSD", "ancientSD", "other")]
anc_ks <- ksw[, .(pairs = .N, median_Ks = median(Ks), below2 = 100 * mean(Ks < 2),
                  window = 100 * mean(Ks > 1.5 & Ks < 2.6)), by = .(node, set)]
anc_ks_w <- dcast(anc_ks, node ~ set, value.var = c("pairs", "median_Ks", "below2", "window"))
anc_tab <- merge(anc_nodes, merge(anc_ev, anc_ks_w, by = "node"), by = "node", sort = FALSE)
anc_show <- anc_tab[, .(node, label, events, ancientSD_pct = round(100 * ancientSD / events),
                        ancientSD_pairs = pairs_ancientSD, median_Ks = round(median_Ks_ancientSD, 2),
                        Ks_below_2 = round(below2_ancientSD, 1),
                        Ks_1.5_2.6 = round(window_ancientSD, 1), Ks_1.5_2.6_other = round(window_other, 1))]
knitr::kable(anc_show, caption = tcap("anc", "Gene-tree duplications that are ancestrally segmental (ancientSD: segmental or neighbourhood-syntenic in at least two descendant genomes) on key branches, and the Ks of their duplicate pairs (Ks 0.05-5). Ks_below_2: % of ancientSD pairs with Ks < 2; Ks_1.5_2.6: % in the window of the Mortierellales Ks component (Section 3), for ancientSD pairs and for the other pairs of the same branch."))
```

```{r anc-ks-fig, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = cap("anc_ks", "Ks distributions (log scale, Ks 0.05-5) of the duplicate pairs of key branches, for ancientSD duplications and for the other duplications of the same branch (density curves). Dotted line: Ks = 2.")}
ksw <- merge(ksw, anc_nodes, by = "node")
ksw[, panel := factor(paste0(node, ": ", label), paste0(anc_nodes$node, ": ", anc_nodes$label))]
ggplot(ksw, aes(Ks, colour = set)) +
  geom_density(adjust = 0.8, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5), labels = c(0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(ancientSD = "#D55E00", other = "grey55"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Ks", y = "Density") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

## Conclusion

```{r conclusion-6-values}
cb <- function(o, col) calib[W == 10 & order == o][[col]]
nw <- function(nd, col) nb_w[node == nd][[col]]
ev12_real <- ev12[run == "real"]
ev12_multi <- ev12_real[, mean(n_genomes >= 2)]
ev12_multi_null <- ev12[run != "real", mean(n_genomes >= 2)]
other <- same[group == "Other"]
n_older_wins <- other[, sum(N12 > own)]
n_n9_lower <- same[, sum(N9 < N12)]
av <- function(nd, col) anc_show[node == nd][[col]]
wgd_genomes <- c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1", "ggRhiOryz1", "gzRhiStol1")
n12_wo_wgd <- 100 * real10[node == "N12" & !genome %in% wgd_genomes, mean(pass)]
top_g <- g12[order(-pct)][1:3]
gname <- function(g) gen$species[match(g, gen$genome)]
rng <- function(v, d = 1) paste(sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), range(v)), collapse = "-")
```

- **The test is specific and sensitive.** With shuffled gene order only
  `r rng(calib[W == 10, chance], 2)`% of pairs pass, whereas
  `r rng(calib[W == 10 & order != "Umbelopsidales", SD], 0)`% of doubletrouble's
  segmental pairs in Mortierellales and Mucorales do (`r tab("nb_calib")`).
- **Many "dispersed" duplicates are eroded segmental duplicates.**
  `r f1(cb("Mucorales", "DD"))`% of the dispersed pairs in Mucorales and
  `r f1(cb("Mortierellales", "DD"))`% in Mortierellales are
  neighbourhood-syntenic, `r round(cb("Mucorales", "DD_over_chance"))` and
  `r round(cb("Mortierellales", "DD_over_chance"))` times the chance rate.
- **The Mucorales-stem duplicates are syntenic far above chance.**
  `r f1(nw("N12", "real_10"))`% of the N12 pairs pass,
  `r round(nw("N12", "real_10") / nw("N12", "chance_10"))` times the chance rate,
  against `r f1(nw("N9", "real_10"))`% for the older N9 duplicates; the result
  holds with the wider windows (`r tab("nb_nodes")`, `r fig("nb_age")`).
  `r f1(nw("N12", "ev_real"))`% of the N12 duplications are syntenic in at
  least one Mucorales genome (chance `r f1(nw("N12", "ev_chance"))`%), and
  `r pct(ev12_multi)`% in two or more (chance `r pct(ev12_multi_null, 1)`%),
  while the same duplications are dispersed in other genomes
  (`r fig("nb_events")`). The genomes that keep the most are those of
  `r paste(sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", gname(top_g$genome), top_g$pct), collapse = ", ")`.
- **They are more syntenic than younger duplicates in the same genomes.** In
  `r n_older_wins` of `r nrow(other)` younger Mucorales nodes (excluding those
  next to the recent WGDs and the *Lichtheimia* signal), the N12 duplicates
  are more often syntenic than the node's own, younger duplicates in the same
  genomes (`r fig("nb_same")`), and the older N9 duplicates are less syntenic
  than the N12 duplicates in `r n_n9_lower` of `r nrow(same)`. Since synteny
  decays with time, the Mucorales-stem duplications must more often have
  arisen as multi-gene duplications than the later duplications in the same
  genomes. The signal does not come from duplicates of the recent WGDs being
  misplaced on N12: without the *Absidia* and *Rhizopus* genomes,
  `r f1(n12_wo_wgd)`% of the N12 pairs are syntenic.
- **Mortierellales.** `r f1(nw("N10", "real_10"))`% of the Mortierellales-stem
  duplicates are neighbourhood-syntenic, more than with the collinearity rule
  (`r f1(100 * nv("N10", "sd_share"))`%), consistent with a large-scale
  duplication early in the order.
- **Ancestrally segmental duplications.** `r av("N12", "ancientSD_pct")`% of the
  Mucorales-stem duplications are ancientSD, but their pairs are saturated
  (median Ks `r av("N12", "median_Ks")`; `r av("N12", "Ks_below_2")`% below 2):
  Ks cannot date this event even when restricted to block duplicates
  (`r tab("anc")`, `r fig("anc_ks")`). On the Mortierellales stem,
  `r av("N10", "ancientSD_pct")`% of the duplications are ancientSD, and their
  pairs are enriched in the Ks 1.5-2.6 window (`r av("N10", "Ks_1.5_2.6")`%
  against `r av("N10", "Ks_1.5_2.6_other")`% for the other stem duplicates), so
  the Ks component shared by all Mortierellales genomes (Section 3) most
  likely reflects this event. If substitution rates are similar in the two orders, it is younger
  than the Mucorales-stem event, perhaps late on the long Mortierellales stem.
- **What this adds.** With collinearity, the Mucorales-stem burst showed no
  sign of block duplication. With an order-free measure it does: its
  duplicates arose in duplicated regions far more often than expected by
  chance and than later duplicates, but are now scattered because gene order
  has been scrambled since. Together with the breadth of the burst and the
  parallel retention of copies (Section 4), this is the evidence for a
  large-scale duplication, most simply a WGD, on the Mucorales stem. It does
  not exclude several large segmental duplications on that branch, which a
  model-based test (e.g. Whale) could address.

# Summary {-}

- **Genome set.** Most of the 61 assemblies are contiguous enough to detect
  collinear duplicates. gzMucFlav4 likely contains duplicated assembly
  sequences, and near-identical pairs are treated separately throughout.
- **Duplicate landscape.** `r round(dup_range[1])`-`r round(dup_range[2])`%
  of genes are in paralogous pairs in each genome, mostly as dispersed
  duplicates. Collinear (segmental) duplicates are common only in
  Mortierellales and in *Absidia* and *Rhizopus*. In other Mucorales and in
  Umbelopsidales they are rare even in chromosome-level assemblies, and in
  Mucorales a large share of them are near-identical.
- **Gene number.** Larger gene sets come mainly from more dispersed
  duplicates, except in *Absidia* and *Rhizopus*, where many extra genes are
  segmental duplicates (candidate lineage-specific WGDs).
- **Recent lineage-specific WGDs.** *Absidia* and *Rhizopus oryzae* have
  segmental Ks peaks at about Ks `r paste(range(round(main_peak[genome %in% abs_rhi, Ks], 1)), collapse = "-")`,
  younger than the split of the two genera, so they are two independent
  events. The *Absidia* event is shared by *A. cylindrospora* and *A. repens*
  (and perhaps *A. glauca*); the *Rhizopus* event is shared by *R. oryzae* and
  *R. stolonifer*, postdates the split from *R. microsporus* and probably
  matches the WGD known from *R. delemar*.
- **The proposed early WGD.** Gene trees show a burst of duplications on the
  Mucorales stem (`r round(nv("N12", "rate") / med_rate, 1)` times the median
  rate), not on the branch shared with Umbelopsidales. The burst is spread
  across many gene families and its copies were retained in parallel across
  Mucorales, as after a WGD. Ks is saturated at that age, there is no
  macrosynteny between the orders for a 1:2 test, and the duplicates are no
  longer collinear: families expanded in Mucorales gained dispersed copies,
  not tandem arrays.
- **Synteny without gene order.** Many "dispersed" duplicates are eroded
  segmental duplicates. Measured without gene order, the Mucorales-stem
  duplicates still lie in duplicated neighbourhoods
  `r round(nw("N12", "real_10") / nw("N12", "chance_10"))` times more often than
  by chance, half of these duplications are syntenic in at least one Mucorales
  genome, and they are more syntenic than younger duplicates in the same
  genomes. They therefore arose in multi-gene duplications, and their
  collinearity was lost later through the scrambling of gene order. With the
  breadth and parallel retention of the burst, this makes a large-scale
  duplication on the Mucorales stem, most simply the WGD proposed by
  Corrochano et al., the best explanation; a model-based test (Whale) could
  still separate a single WGD from several large segmental duplications.
  Families expanded in *Absidia* and *Rhizopus* are still largely in
  collinear blocks.
- **Mortierellales.** Collinear and neighbourhood-syntenic duplicates mapped
  to the Mortierellales stem and earliest nodes, and collinear expansions of
  gene families, suggest a large-scale duplication on the Mortierellales stem.
  Its ancestrally segmental duplicates make up the Ks component near 2.4
  shared by all Mortierellales genomes, whereas those of the Mucorales stem
  are saturated, so the Mortierellales event is probably the younger of the
  two.
